title: Title: Geometric Quantum State Representation & Manipulation
abstract: Quantum state representation and manipulation represent a fundamental challenge in quantum information science. Current methods often struggle with precision and scalability, hindering the development of complex quantum algorithms. This paper proposes a novel geometric representation for quantum states, leveraging entanglement and geometric operations to achieve unprecedented control and manipulation capabilities. The core mechanism centers around defining a 'Quantum State Vector' – a vector representing the state's geometry – allowing for precise transformation and manipulation through a combination of quantum entanglement and geometric transformations. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through rigorous mathematical analysis and illustrative examples, highlighting its potential to surpass current limitations in quantum state manipulation.

title: ## The Mimicry-Guided Adaptive Search (MGAS) Algorithm: An Inspiration from Short-tailed Atheris
abstract: This paper introduces the Mimicry-Guided Adaptive Search (MGAS) algorithm, a novel metaheuristic optimization technique inspired by the foraging behavior and camouflage strategies of the short-tailed Atheris (short-tailed shrew). The algorithm leverages the principle of mimicry – the short-tailed Atheris's ability to imitate successful foraging patterns of other individuals – combined with adaptive parameter adjustment to navigate complex search spaces. MGAS employs a population-based approach, where each individual represents a potential solution. The algorithm's core mechanism involves mimicking successful solutions within the population, dynamically adjusting the mimicry rate and exploration/exploitation balance based on the diversity and convergence characteristics of the population. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through theoretical analysis, demonstrating its potential for efficient exploration and exploitation in various optimization problems. Key features include a dynamic mimicry ratio, a population diversity preservation mechanism, and an adaptive step size control.

title: AI-Driven Marketing Analytics for Predicting Customer Preferences for Eco-Friendly Excavators in the Indian Construction Equipment Market
abstract: Abstract The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into marketing is transforming the way organisations understand customer preferences, predict buying behaviour and design personalised marketing strategies. In the construction equipment industry, increasing environmental concerns, emission requirements and demand for fuel-efficient technologies have created a need for more effective approaches to promote eco-friendly excavators. This study proposes an empirical investigation of the role of AI-driven marketing analytics in predicting customer preferences for eco-friendly excavators in the Indian construction equipment market. Drawing upon the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and the Antecedents-Decisions-Outcomes (ADO) framework, the study examines the influence of AI-enabled personalisation, predictive analytics, environmental awareness and perceived usefulness of AI-based recommendations on customer preference for eco-friendly excavators. The study focuses on construction contractors, equipment purchasers and other industrial decision-makers involved in excavator procurement. A structured questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale is proposed for primary data collection. Descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlation and regression analysis can be employed to examine the proposed relationships. The study contributes to sustainable marketing literature by connecting AI-driven marketing analytics with industrial customer preferences in the heavy construction equipment sector. The empirical statistics reported in this manuscript are based on a simulated dataset of 212 respondents and are intended for demonstration only.

title: Beyond Suspicion Scores: Competing-Explanation Inference for Fraud-Shaped Legitimate Activity
abstract: Fraud detection systems commonly score suspiciousness and act when a score crosses a threshold. This is unreliable when legitimate activity exhibits fraud-like structure: in our diagnostic corpus, structurally suspicious legitimate cases carry more fraud-shaped relational structure than genuine fraud does, and every purely structural statistic we evaluated ranked them above fraud. We present AFIE, a knowledge-based evidentiary architecture that treats fraud recognition as adjudication between competing explanations rather than accumulation of suspicion. A case likelihood is composed on a bounded log-odds scale as L0 + F + M - B - C, combining affirmative fraud-semantic evidence (F) grouped into coherent mechanisms, gated mature recognition (M), affirmative exculpatory evidence (B), and contradiction evidence (C). The architecture is recomputed from the current evidence state at each observation prefix, has no absorbing state, and treats the absence of exculpatory evidence as contributing exactly zero. Its principal contribution is an evidentiary admissibility rule for mature recognition: a completed exemplar is admitted only when it is persistent, positively informative relative to locally estimated ordinary opportunity, a member of the coherent mechanism selected by the affirmative channel, situated in a mechanism whose net evidence supports fraud, and not covered by applicable exculpatory evidence. On a 160-case authored all-comers corpus with semantically adequate documentary evidence, the architecture attains an area under the ROC curve of 0.904 at the final prefix, with final-prefix AUC 0.904 (95% bootstrap CI [0.847, 0.952]), complete mature-fraud detection, zero observed escalation across both legitimate families, 4.3% dangerous under-detection, and 0/1,600 prefix-isolation leakage violations. We report negative findings in full, including the failure of graph-coherence formulations and of an emerging-before-mature hypothesis. The evaluation is a local mechanism proof on an authored corpus and is not independent validation.

title: A Computational Framework for Cross-Temporal Sentiment and Topic Analysis of Reddit Data
abstract: This paper develops and validates a modular computational framework for longitudinal sentiment and thematic analysis of unstructured social media data. While computational social science increasingly relies on automated tools, a gap remains in validated pipelines that rigorously integrate temporal dynamics with reliable sentiment metrics for noisy text. The proposed technical contribution is a three-stage pipeline comprising: (1) a comparative validation protocol establishing the superiority of lexicon-based rules (VADER) over un-tuned transformers (BERT) for specific informal domains; (2) a hybrid hierarchical topic modeling approach; and (3) a robust regression architecture cross-validated with LightGBM machine learning models. The framework's engineering utility is demonstrated through a 15-year dataset (N = 2267) of cross-cultural Reddit discourse. Results confirm the pipeline's ability to reliably detect event-driven signal shifts and isolate feature importance. This study offers engineers and data scientists a validated, replicable solution for high-noise public opinion mining and crisis monitoring applications.

title: A Study on LLM-based Game NPC State Control using FSM
abstract: 최근 LLM(Large Language Model)을 활용한 게임 NPC는 플레이어의 자연어 입력에 따라 유연하고 자연스러운 대화를 제공할 수 있다. 그러나 LLM 기반 NPC의 자유로운 응답은 현재 게임 상태나 기획 의도와 맞지 않는 행동으로 이어질 수 있으며, 거래, 퀘스트, 보상, 전투와 같은 시스템과 연결될 경우 비허용 상태 전이가 발생할 수 있다. 본 논문에서는 LLM 기반 NPC의 대화 능력을 유지하면서도, 게임 규칙을 벗어난 행동이 실제 시스템에 반영되지 않도록 FSM 기반 가드레일 구조를 제안한다. 제안 구조는 LLM이 플레이어 입력을 JSON 형식의 intent와 ruleTags로 변환하고, FSM이 현재 게임 상태와 규칙을 검증한 뒤 상태 전이 허용 여부를 결정하는 방식이다. Unity 기반 NPC 상호작용 환경에서 LLM-only 방식과 LLM+FSM 방식을 비교한 결과, 비허용 입력에 대한 금지 상태 전이의 발생을 감소시켰으며, 정상 입력의 성공률을 향상시켰다.

title: One note in three: a verified census of three deployed AI scribes, and the instrument that counted it
abstract: Ambient AI scribes draft clinical notes under the reassurance that a clinician signs every note. We audited three commercial AI scribes on the same 142 consultations: 565 notes from recorded UK primary-care and US ambulatory encounters plus authored scenarios. Twelve discovery passes proposed 13,678 candidate errors; the 5,898 clearing an importance filter went to an adversarial panel of two models from different families, each told to refute what it could, and 618 survived. One note in three (31.3% [27.0, 35.6]) carries a verified failure, concentrated in allergy and medication information, invented patient identity, and history written up as examination on telephone consultations that can contain none. No product was given a patient record; setting aside the two classes a record would have prefilled, invented identity and dates, the rate is 24.8% [20.8, 29.0]. One failure mode did not fit our scheme, drawn from published scribe-error taxonomies: a treatment the clinician retracts, recorded as delivered care. Two clinicians adjudicated blind, disjoint samples: a physician author upheld 20 of 21 findings (95.2% [77.3, 99.2]) and an independent clinician, not an author, 12 of 12 ([75.8, 100]); both judged every sampled refusal genuine. A failure rate depends on the instrument as much as the scribes. With model, evidence and settings fixed, the review instruction alone moves the share of candidates verified from 9.3% to 79.0%, and the reviewing family moves it too: alone at that instruction the gentler flags 54.8% of notes against 27.8%. Between 28% and 97% of sampled notes carry a failure depending on the standard. Published audits disagree among themselves by a margin instrument differences alone can produce: omission is 54-86% of their errors against our 23.1%. We release all 618 findings with transcript-side evidence, every prompt and model version, and the re-runnable pipeline.

title: Machine Learning-based Virtual Densification of Sparse Environmental Variables (Solar Radiation and PM10) from Co-located Basic Weather Observations across South Korea
abstract: Among the weather networks in South Korea, although basic variables are recorded at 600 to 744 stations nationwide, only approximately 67 and 31 are equipped with sensors for detecting solar radiation (GSR) and particulate matter (PM10), respectively. Exploiting this asymmetry, we propose a machine-learning-based virtual densification to facilitate estimations of sparse variables from co-located basic-weather variables, evaluated based on leave-station-out (LSO) cross-validation, excluding entire stations to emulate sensor-free locations. Solar radiation was found to be effectively densified (LSO R2 = 0.76 ± 0.03), far exceeding the Hargreaves-Samani baseline (R2 = 0.54) and was stable without coordinates, indicating a physical relationship. Comparatively, PM10 reaches only R2 = 0.28 from weather alone, a control for emission-driven variables. Although machine learning (RandomForest, XGBoost) achieves significantly higher predictive accuracy than the empirical and linear baselines (p < 0.001), the two models are mutually indistinguishable. Given that solar radiation is a required wet-bulb globe temperature input, the virtual solar field can directly support heat-disaster risk assessment in locations in which sensors are absent.

title: Non-Linear Geometric Topology Quantum Algorithms
abstract: This paper explores the application of non-linear geometric topology in quantum algorithms to enhance computational efficiency and uncover novel geometric features. The core focus is on leveraging quantum entanglement and self-adaptive mechanisms to devise quantum algorithms that surpass classical limitations. We investigate how these techniques can facilitate the manipulation of complex geometric structures, ultimately leading to significant improvements in data analysis and computational speed. The study aims to identify specific geometric patterns and their associated quantum properties, offering a pathway toward advancements in data processing and potentially revolutionizing computational paradigms.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Probability Model
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic adaptive probability model, designed to address the limitations of traditional probability models in dynamic environments. The model employs a dynamic probability update mechanism, driven by learning data and environmental information, to dynamically adjust model parameters and automatically learn new model structures. This allows for more accurate predictions and decisions in real-time. The core mechanism centers around a learning-based parameter adjustment process, combined with reinforcement learning techniques for structural adaptation. The benefits of this approach include enhanced adaptability, improved predictive accuracy, and automated model refinement. This work presents a framework for creating a model capable of continuous learning and optimization across diverse scenarios.

title: Meta-Learning for Continual Learning: A Rapid Adaptation Framework
abstract: This paper proposes a novel continual learning framework based on meta-learning, designed to facilitate rapid adaptation of models across diverse tasks. Traditional continual learning methods often struggle with the inherent variability between tasks, frequently relying on techniques like transfer learning that can be sensitive to task differences. Our approach leverages the core principle of meta-learning – learning *how* to learn – to enable the model to efficiently acquire knowledge and generalize across a sequence of tasks. The framework utilizes meta-learning algorithms to optimize the learning process itself, leading to improved performance and reduced catastrophic forgetting. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical analysis and outline the key components, focusing on the adaptive learning rate and task-specific regularization strategies within the meta-learning loop. The resulting system offers a more robust and efficient solution for continual learning compared to conventional methods.

title: 基于生物神经网络的计算生物学模型优化
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to optimizing computational biology models by leveraging the principles of biological neural networks. Traditional methods for model optimization often rely on heuristic search algorithms and manual parameter tuning, which can be computationally expensive and yield suboptimal results. Our approach transforms computational biology models into a network of interconnected weights, analogous to the connections in a biological neural network. We then utilize adaptive learning algorithms inspired by biological neural networks to iteratively refine these weights, aiming to improve model accuracy and efficiency. The core of this method lies in the mapping of the model's parameters and structure to a neural network architecture, allowing for the exploitation of the inherent learning capabilities of biological systems. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a conceptual framework, outlining the key steps involved and highlighting the advantages over conventional optimization techniques. This work provides a foundation for future research exploring the integration of biological neural network optimization strategies within the field of computational biology.

title: Title: Adaptive Topology for Quantum Simulation of Condensed Matter
abstract: Quantum simulation of condensed matter systems offers unprecedented insights into their behavior, but current methods often struggle to accurately represent the complex dynamics and intricate topologies. This paper introduces an adaptive topology framework for quantum simulation, aiming to overcome these limitations. We propose a novel algorithm that dynamically adjusts the topology of the quantum simulation space during the simulation process, guided by the system's dynamics. This adaptation significantly improves the representation of the underlying physics, leading to enhanced accuracy and robustness. The core mechanism leverages a feedback loop that continuously evaluates the topology and refines it to achieve optimal representation. This approach promises a significant advancement in quantum simulation capabilities, particularly for complex systems exhibiting intricate topologies.

title: Quantum Entanglement's Adaptive Quantum Algorithm
abstract: This paper explores the potential of adaptive quantum algorithms, leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement, to revolutionize quantum computation. We introduce a novel framework centered on dynamically adjusting quantum parameters in response to input data, aiming to enhance computational efficiency. The core mechanism involves utilizing self-adjusting entanglement to achieve this dynamic adjustment. The research presents a theoretical foundation and a preliminary implementation demonstrating the framework's capabilities. The work addresses a critical challenge in quantum algorithm design: the need for flexible and adaptive solutions.

We introduce a novel framework centered on dynamically adjusting quantum parameters in response to input data, aiming to enhance computational efficiency. The core mechanism involves utilizing self-adjusting entanglement to achieve this dynamic adjustment. The research presents a theoretical foundation and a preliminary implementation demonstrating the framework's capabilities. The work addresses a critical challenge in quantum algorithm design: the need for flexible and adaptive solutions.

title: Self-Adaptive Entropy Calculation and Application
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive entropy calculation method designed to enhance data compression efficiency and information retrieval speed. Traditional entropy estimation techniques are often static, failing to adequately adapt to the varying characteristics of input data. Our approach dynamically adjusts entropy levels based on data features, providing a more responsive and efficient solution. We present a methodology incorporating a feedback loop that iteratively refines the entropy estimation process. The core mechanism centers around a dynamic entropy adjustment algorithm, ensuring optimal performance across diverse datasets. This work offers a significant advancement in entropy estimation, potentially revolutionizing data compression and retrieval processes.

title: Quantum Simulation-Driven Materials Discovery
abstract: This paper explores the transformative potential of quantum simulation for accelerating materials discovery. Classical computational methods often struggle with the complexities of simulating quantum mechanical systems, particularly for materials exhibiting strong electron correlations. Quantum simulation offers a fundamentally different approach, leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics to directly model these systems on a quantum computer. This work outlines the key concepts, methodologies, and potential impact of this emerging field. We present a framework for utilizing quantum computers to simulate material properties, including electronic structure, magnetic behavior, and transport characteristics. Specifically, we discuss the use of Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) and Trotterization methods for solving the Schrödinger equation. The core claim is that quantum simulation will revolutionize materials discovery by enabling precise predictions of material properties and accelerating the identification of novel materials with desired characteristics. Furthermore, we address the current limitations and future directions of this technology, emphasizing the need for robust quantum hardware and sophisticated algorithms. ---

title: Quantum-Enhanced Bayesian Inference for Optimization
abstract: Quantum-enhanced Bayesian inference offers a promising approach to accelerate optimization of complex, high-dimensional problems, particularly those plagued by noisy data. This paper investigates the potential of leveraging quantum annealing or variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) to dramatically improve the speed and efficiency of optimization. We explore the core mechanism of utilizing these quantum algorithms to efficiently explore the solution space, addressing the limitations of classical optimization techniques. The paper begins with a review of Bayesian inference, its challenges, and the potential benefits of quantum computing. It then delves into the specific application of quantum annealing and VQE to optimization, highlighting key advantages in terms of exploration and convergence. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future directions of this research, emphasizing the need for further investigation and development.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum-enhanced algorithm for topology computation, leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement to achieve significantly improved precision. Traditional topological computation methods often struggle with the complexity of intricate structures, hindering their application to real-world problems. The core mechanism involves constructing a quantum state representing the topology, utilizing entanglement to facilitate precise manipulation and computation. The algorithm's efficacy is demonstrated through a series of examples, showcasing its capacity to tackle complex topological structures with enhanced accuracy.

title: ## The Bio-Inspired Harmony Search Algorithm for Multi-Objective Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces the Harmony Search Algorithm (HSA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of tiger prawn ( *Penaeus monodon* ). The algorithm mimics the prawns' harmonious search for food sources, utilizing a harmony pool, a harmony memory, and a dynamic harmony adjustment mechanism. The core principle lies in the prawns' ability to identify and select the best food sources within their environment through a process of iterative refinement and harmonic convergence. The HSA aims to address the challenges of traditional metaheuristic algorithms by incorporating a more robust exploration-exploitation balance and a mechanism for adapting to complex, multi-dimensional search spaces. This paper details the algorithm's design, operational principles, and theoretical foundations, highlighting its potential applicability across various optimization problems. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a conceptual analysis, focusing on its adaptability and convergence characteristics, without requiring empirical experimentation.

title: Title: Self-Aware Geometric Networks for Pattern Recognition
abstract: This paper explores the application of Self-Aware Geometric Networks (SANGs) to pattern recognition, a novel approach leveraging the influence of neighbors within a network topology. The core claim is to design a network architecture where nodes are dynamically influenced by their neighbors, fostering a system capable of recognizing patterns through geometric relationships. We propose a novel network design that incorporates a proximity-based influence mechanism, allowing nodes to adjust their output based on the proximity of nearby nodes. This allows for a more robust and adaptable pattern recognition system. The paper details the network topology, the influence mechanism, and the resulting performance evaluation, demonstrating the effectiveness of SANGs in identifying complex patterns.

title: Quantum Resource Allocation Based on Quantum Demagnetization
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to optimizing quantum computing resource allocation, leveraging the inherent characteristics of quantum demagnetization (decoherence). Traditional quantum resource allocation methods often rely on heuristic rules or empirical observations, lacking a fundamental understanding of the resource consumption mechanisms within a quantum system. This work posits that decoherence, a primary source of error and resource depletion in quantum computation, can be explicitly modeled and utilized as a constraint within an optimization framework. We present a methodology for allocating quantum resources—specifically, qubit assignments and gate scheduling—based on a dynamic assessment of decoherence rates. The core concept involves formulating a mathematical model where decoherence is treated as a cost function, and employing optimization algorithms to minimize this cost while satisfying computational requirements. The proposed method offers a potentially more efficient and targeted approach to resource allocation, leading to improvements in quantum computation efficiency and potentially mitigating the detrimental effects of decoherence. The results demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this approach in theoretical scenarios.

title: ## The Coral Horn Optimization Algorithm: A Biomimetic Approach Inspired by Ram Horn Coral
abstract: This paper introduces the Coral Horn Optimization Algorithm (CHOA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the unique morphology and foraging behavior of *Ram Horn Coral* (Axinella corallina). The algorithm leverages the coral's ability to efficiently navigate complex environments by strategically adjusting the angles and lengths of its horn-like structures, mimicking a dynamic adaptation strategy. CHOA utilizes a population-based search, employing a novel horn representation, an adaptive angle adjustment mechanism, and a dynamic length scaling factor to explore and exploit the search space. The algorithm's core innovation lies in its ability to maintain a diverse and adaptable population, promoting efficient convergence towards optimal solutions. This paper outlines the algorithm's principles, mathematical formulation, and potential applications, emphasizing its potential advantages over existing metaheuristic methods.

title: Title: Non-Local Quantum Wave Function Propagation
abstract: Quantum wave function propagation, while foundational to quantum mechanics, often struggles to capture intricate correlations and complex patterns. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, the 'Quantum Network Propagation' method, designed to overcome these limitations by facilitating instantaneous transmission of quantum information across interconnected quantum systems. We demonstrate the algorithm's ability to generate and maintain correlated quantum states far exceeding traditional propagation techniques, opening the door to exploring novel quantum phenomena and potentially revolutionizing quantum information processing. The core mechanism centers around establishing a dynamic, interconnected quantum network, enabling the propagation of information through a multitude of entangled states. This research explores the potential for creating non-local correlations, a critical aspect for many quantum applications, and provides a foundational framework for further investigation.

title: ## Algerian Mouse: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of Algerian Mice
abstract: This paper introduces Algerian Mouse, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Algerian mice. These mice are known for their efficient and adaptive search strategies in complex environments. The algorithm, termed Algerian Mouse (AM), leverages concepts such as scent marking, spatial memory, and exploratory movement to achieve robust optimization performance. AM employs a population-based approach, utilizing a 'nest' representation to simulate the mice's social dynamics and a 'trail' mechanism to mimic scent marking and spatial memory. The algorithm's core components include a 'nest' formation process, a 'trail' discovery and maintenance mechanism, and a movement strategy based on probabilistic exploration. We present a detailed description of the algorithm's mechanics, along with its theoretical foundations. The performance of AM is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive advantages compared to established metaheuristic methods such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Genetic Algorithm (GA). The results indicate that AM offers a promising approach for tackling challenging optimization problems, particularly those involving complex landscapes and dynamic environments. Future research will focus on refining the algorithm's parameters and exploring its applicability in diverse domains.

title: When AI Says It Is Not Sure: AI Uncertainty Expression, Trust, and Purchase Hesitation in Online Health Product Recommendation
abstract: AI recommendation assistants increasingly provide quasi-advisory support in online health-product shopping, yet little is known about how their expressions of uncertainty shape consumer decisions. Drawing on the stimulus–organism–response framework, signaling theory, and computer-mediated communication/Computers Are Social Actors logic, this study conceptualizes AI uncertainty expression (AIUE) as a message-level cue of epistemic certainty. A 2 (AIUE: high vs. low) × 2 (health risk severity: high vs. low) between-subjects experiment with 599 online consumers showed that AIUE reduced competence trust and benevolence trust and increased purchase hesitation. Trait indecisiveness moderated both trust-formation paths: the negative effects of AIUE were stronger among consumers low in indecisiveness. Conditional indirect-effect analyses showed that competence trust transmitted the effect at both low and high indecisiveness, whereas benevolence trust did so only at low indecisiveness. The focal model was estimated in a design containing both mild and more serious HRS contexts. Because the manipulation also shifted perceived recommendation strength, helpfulness, and informativeness, the downstream effects should be interpreted as responses to naturally expressed uncertainty rather than to an isolated certainty cue. These findings extend research on AI-mediated communication by showing how uncertainty wording shapes distinct trust judgments and purchase hesitation and by identifying trait indecisiveness as a boundary condition.

title: LLM Judges Verify Presence, Not Absence: Omission Blindness in AI Clinical Notes and What Recovers It
abstract: Ambient AI scribes draft clinical notes, and published audits find their dominant error is omission: information the encounter established that the note fails to record. The standard check is an LLM judge: a second model reads the note against the transcript and flags problems. We ask whether judges detect omissions. Public corpora cannot supply the answer key: their clinician reference notes and transcripts are materially discrepant. Our benchmark has 500 single-error note pairs from audited fact sheets, 298 with a named fact certainly absent and 202 added-or-altered controls. Across eight judge designs, paired discrimination (the flawed note below its clean twin, 0.5 a coin flip) reads 0.79-0.94 on added or altered content and 0.50-0.63 on omissions. On single notes, no design flags omissions reliably more often than perfect notes. Wording changes, voting and GEPA prompt optimisation move the operating point without creating usable detection. Restructuring the task recovers it: list the facts the transcript establishes, then check the note for each. Two methods reach it independently and trade off: a per-fact pipeline, and a GEPA-evolved prompt doing the same in one call. The pipeline's flags name the missing fact and its severity at 2.7% false alarms. The single call detects more (36.9% against 24.6%, p=0.002) at 6.2% false alarms and a tenth of the cost per note. A physician author validated 70 items and, where the two routes disagree, sided with the pipeline on 10 of 10 (p=0.002). A second clinician, not an author, graded the severity rubric blind and agrees to within a grade. On real vendor notes from a companion census no benchmark threshold transfers, but the re-calibrated single call detects more than the best of the eight at half its false-alarm rate. Omissions whose fact is restated elsewhere defeat both routes. We release the benchmark, prompts and judgements.

title: Quantum Programming Landscape Catalog
abstract: A catalog of 101 quantum software artifacts — languages, SDKs, intermediate representations, compilers, simulators, control frameworks, domain libraries, and cloud execution services — each classified by its role in the quantum software stack and scored on ten dimensions of suitability for autonomous, agent-mediated programming and execution. The workbook implements the Agentic Quantum Readiness Score (AQRS) end to end: every component score, weighted total, tier, lifecycle adjustment, and deployment-readiness value is a live spreadsheet formula over audited inputs, so any published number can be traced backward to the classification and source document that produced it. Each row records its primary evidence URL, the date that source was last fetched, and a verdict stating whether the fetched page substantively describes the artifact rather than merely resolving.

title: 基于自适应的超参数调整的神经网络
abstract: This paper presents a novel neural network architecture, termed the Adaptive Hyperparameter Tuning Neural Network (AHTN), designed to optimize neural network hyperparameters through an adaptive learning process. Traditional hyperparameter tuning methods often struggle to effectively adapt to the specific characteristics of the training data, leading to suboptimal model performance and increased training times. The AHTN leverages a self-adaptive learning algorithm that iteratively adjusts hyperparameters based on the observed training data distribution, achieving a more robust and efficient hyperparameter optimization strategy. We explore the benefits of this approach in improving model accuracy and reducing training duration, demonstrating its effectiveness through theoretical analysis and experimental validation.

title: Dynamic Self-Organizing Neural Networks
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic self-organizing neural network architecture designed to adapt to changing input data in real-time. Traditional neural networks often rely on static weights and parameters, limiting their ability to effectively learn and generalize. Our proposed network utilizes a dynamic adjustment mechanism to restructure the network structure and weights, allowing it to continuously update its parameters based on the incoming data. This dynamic adaptation fosters more efficient learning and improved performance compared to static models. The core principle behind this design is the iterative process of adjusting network parameters to minimize prediction error and maximize the network's ability to maintain accuracy as input data shifts. We present a rigorous theoretical analysis demonstrating the effectiveness of this dynamic adjustment mechanism and highlight its potential applications in various domains.

title: Black Mastiff Bat: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of Black Mastiff Bats
abstract: This paper introduces the Black Mastiff Bat (BMB) algorithm, a novel metaheuristic optimization technique inspired by the unique foraging strategies of Black Mastiff bats ( *Lasiurus cinereus*). Unlike traditional metaheuristic approaches, BMB incorporates a dynamic obstacle avoidance mechanism and a sophisticated path-planning system mimicking the bats' ability to navigate complex environments and efficiently locate food sources. The algorithm utilizes a population of bats, each represented by a position and velocity vector, to explore the search space. A central 'food' source is defined, and each bat attempts to reach it while simultaneously avoiding dynamically generated obstacles. The obstacle avoidance mechanism is based on the bats' echolocation, implemented through a distance-based repulsion force. Path planning incorporates a 'leading' bat that strategically guides the population towards promising regions, enhancing convergence speed. The BMB algorithm's performance is evaluated through simulations on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential advantages over established metaheuristics. The key components of the algorithm are detailed, including the obstacle generation process, the leading bat strategy, and the velocity update rules. The results demonstrate the algorithm's robustness and adaptability, suggesting its applicability in diverse optimization scenarios. The core innovation lies in the integration of dynamic obstacle avoidance and strategic path planning, directly inspired by the observed behavior of Black Mastiff bats.

title: Meta-Learning for Few-Shot Relational Reasoning in Knowledge Graphs
abstract: This paper investigates the application of meta-learning techniques to address the challenge of few-shot relational reasoning within knowledge graphs (KGs). Existing approaches often fail to generalize effectively when faced with novel relational reasoning tasks requiring minimal training data. We propose a novel meta-learning algorithm designed to rapidly adapt to new tasks by exploiting inherent structural knowledge of KGs. Our method learns a meta-learner that effectively utilizes prior knowledge about graph structures and relationships to quickly acquire the necessary skills for relational reasoning. We formalize the problem as a meta-learning scenario, focusing on learning how to learn relational reasoning. The key components of the algorithm include a base learner, a meta-learner, and a knowledge graph embedding module. We define the learning objective as minimizing the error rate on unseen relational reasoning tasks after only a few training examples. The core of our approach lies in the meta-learner's ability to efficiently update its parameters based on the limited feedback received during task adaptation. We provide a detailed mathematical formulation of the meta-learning process and discuss the key design choices. The results, though not presented through empirical experiments due to the focus on the theoretical framework, illustrate the potential of our approach to significantly improve the generalization capabilities of meta-learning algorithms in the context of few-shot relational reasoning in KGs.

title: # Big Pocket Gopher: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of the Big-Pocketed Gopher
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Big Pocket Gopher (BPG), inspired by the foraging strategies of the big-pocketed gopher ( *Spalax musstoffianus*). These subterranean rodents are known for their efficient and adaptive burrowing behavior, specifically their ability to locate and exploit food resources over considerable distances. BPG leverages this natural intelligence through a modified Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) framework. The algorithm incorporates a 'pocket' concept, representing a memory of previously visited and evaluated solutions. Solutions are evaluated based on their 'pocket' value – a weighted average of their fitness and distance from the current best solution. The core innovation lies in dynamically adjusting the weight of the 'pocket' value, influenced by the algorithm's convergence rate and the diversity of the population. This adaptive weighting scheme aims to balance exploitation of promising solutions and exploration of the search space. We demonstrate the effectiveness of BPG through simulations on benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The key contributions of this work are the introduction of the 'pocket' concept and the adaptive weighting scheme, which significantly enhance the search efficiency and robustness of the algorithm.

title: Explainable Quantum Computing Model
abstract: Quantum computing presents a paradigm shift in computation, offering the potential to solve problems intractable for classical computers. However, the inherent complexity of quantum mechanics poses a significant challenge: the lack of interpretability. This paper introduces an Explainable Quantum Computing Model (EQCM), built upon the foundations of probability logic and information theory, designed to provide a transparent understanding of quantum computation processes and outcomes. The model aims to bridge the gap between the abstract nature of quantum algorithms and human intuition. We propose a framework where quantum operations are represented and interpreted within a probabilistic logic framework, allowing for the tracing and explanation of quantum state transformations. The core of the EQCM lies in quantifying uncertainty and leveraging information theory to derive explanations for observed quantum behaviors. This work contributes to the growing field of quantum explainability, paving the way for improved debugging, validation, and ultimately, wider adoption of quantum computing technologies. The model's key features include a probabilistic representation of quantum states, a formal method for tracking quantum operations, and a mechanism for quantifying the degree of uncertainty associated with quantum outcomes. We demonstrate how this framework can be applied to simple quantum algorithms, providing insights into their underlying mechanisms.

title: Anatolian Vole-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (AVMOA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, Anatolian Vole-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (AVMOA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Anatolian vole. The algorithm leverages the vole's efficient search strategy for food resources, specifically focusing on its movement patterns and decision-making processes when faced with limited resources and uncertainty. AVMOA combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Cauchy-Matthewmann Mutation (CMM) to create a robust and adaptive optimization technique. The core of AVMOA lies in its 'Foraging Radius' parameter, which dynamically adjusts based on the perceived density of potential solutions, mimicking the vole's exploration and exploitation strategy. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in achieving high solution quality and computational efficiency. Specifically, we explore the algorithm's performance with the following key elements: Initial population initialization (denoted as (s_1, s_2, ..., s_N)), Velocity update equations (v_i(t+1) = w * v_i(t) + c1 * rand() * (pbest_i - x_i(t)) + c2 * rand() * (gbest - x_i(t)), where *i* represents the individual particle, *t* is the iteration number, *w* is the inertia weight, *c1* and *c2* are acceleration coefficients, *rand()* is a random number between 0 and 1, *pbest_i* is the best position found by particle *i* itself, and *gbest* is the best position found by the entire swarm), Adaptive Foraging Radius (RF) calculation (RF(t) = α * (average_distance_to_solution - threshold), where α is a scaling factor, average_distance_to_solution is the average distance of all particles to their nearest solution, and threshold is a predefined minimum distance), and Cauchy-Matthewmann Mutation (CMM) implementation (x_i(t+1) = x_i(t) + F * rand() * (μ - x_i(t)), where F is the mutation constant, μ is the random value drawn from a Cauchy distribution, and rand() is a random number between 0 and 1). The results consistently demonstrate AVMOA's superiority over standard PSO in terms of convergence speed and solution accuracy.

title: Algorithmic Complexity Reduction in Genetic Algorithms for Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the potential for algorithmic complexity reduction in genetic algorithms (GAs) to accelerate optimization of complex problems. Traditional GAs can suffer from high computational costs, particularly with large search spaces. We propose a novel approach, termed "Complexity Reduction," which systematically prunes the search space during the optimization process, thereby minimizing the computational burden and enabling faster convergence. The core mechanism focuses on identifying and eliminating unnecessary parameters or regions of the search space without significantly impacting the solution quality. The paper details the design of this mechanism, its implementation within a GA framework, and provides preliminary results demonstrating a significant reduction in computational time compared to existing approaches for a specific optimization task. The benefits of this approach are discussed, addressing its potential impact on scalability and applicability to a wider range of problems.

title: Allen's Leaf-nosed Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Bio-Acoustic Navigation
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Leaf-nosed Bat Algorithm" (LBA), inspired by the unique navigation strategies employed by Allen's leaf-nosed bats ( *Micronycteris megalotis* ). These bats utilize a sophisticated combination of echolocation and spatial memory to navigate complex environments, particularly in dark cave systems. The LBA algorithm leverages key aspects of this bio-acoustic navigation, including pulse-echo characteristics, spatial mapping, and a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance, to achieve effective optimization. The algorithm incorporates three core mechanisms: a pulse-echo representation of the search space, a spatial memory network for storing promising solutions, and a dynamic adjustment of exploration and exploitation parameters based on the received echo strength. The algorithm is designed for a wide range of optimization problems, including continuous and discrete spaces, and is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and illustrative examples. The LBA algorithm offers a potentially competitive alternative to existing metaheuristic methods, particularly in problems where spatial reasoning and dynamic adaptation are crucial. The algorithm's performance is evaluated against established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) on benchmark functions. Preliminary results suggest that LBA exhibits robust convergence properties and competitive performance, highlighting its potential for future research and applications.

title: Investigating Whether Summarizing Raw Clinical Text Affects the Prediction of In-Hospital Violence: A Retrospective Case Study: Évaluation de l’effet du résumé des textes cliniques bruts sur la prédiction de la violence en milieu hospitalier : étude de cas rétrospective
abstract: BackgroundWe evaluated whether summaries and large language models (LLMs) preserve predictive performance for inpatient violence risk and assessed performance across demographics.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective study of inpatient encounters at Harborview Medical Center between March 2021 and September 2023. Cases were inpatient behavioural violence events, and each was matched to 10 control encounters. For each encounter, we used clinical notes from the 72 hours before the event for cases and a matched window for controls. We compared Clinical-Longformer trained on original notes with pipelines that first generated summaries and then classified risk. Summaries were either general or guided by clinician-defined risk entities. We also tested Llama-3.1-8B and MedGemma-27B in zero-shot (ZS) and fine-tuned settings. Primary endpoints were positive-class precision, recall, and F1. We also reported overall and subgroup area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) with bootstrap confidence intervals for sex, race, ethnicity, age, and mental health flag.ResultsClinical-Longformer on original notes achieved the strongest performance (F1 = 0.776, AUROC = 0.959). Replacing original notes with general or entity-guided summaries reduced performance (F1 = 0.465 and 0.510). Llama-3.1-8B improved with sequence-classification fine-tuning on original notes but remained below Clinical-Longformer (F1 = 0.701; AUROC = 0.933), while ZS prompting performed poorly. MedGemma-27B also remained inferior, with its best performance from sequence-classification fine-tuning on original notes (F1 = 0.612, AUROC = 0.947). Subgroup AUROCs were high across sex, race, ethnicity, and age, with lower performance among patients with a documented mental health flag.ConclusionDirect classification of original notes remained the most reliable strategy. Summaries of clinical notes may compress or alter cues needed for discrimination, and off-the-shelf prompting was inadequate as a stand-alone predictor. A practical path is to anchor risk scoring in long-context discriminative models and use LLMs for auditable, clinician-facing summaries or rationales. Prospective and external validation are needed before clinical deployment.

title: Stick to What You Know: A Study of Knowledge-Aligned Supervised Fine-Tuning
abstract: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) trains a base language model to imitate target responses, and these targets may require knowledge the base model has not robustly internalized. We study this as a source of hallucinations and frame a group of mitigation methods as knowledge-aligned SFT: constraining SFT training targets to the base model's parametric knowledge. Under a unified setup, we compare existing generation-based and estimation-based knowledge-alignment methods and introduce two new variants: Evidence Rewrite, which verifies base-model generations using external evidence, and Recall Rewrite, which retains claims only when they can be consistently recalled by the base model. Experiments with Qwen 3 4B and OLMo 3 7B show that knowledge-aligned SFT can reduce factual hallucinations on WildHalu and Biography while largely preserving general capabilities. Recall Rewrite yields the strongest factuality gains and improves refusal behavior on UnknownBench. It thereby confirms that SFT targets beyond the base model's knowledge drive hallucination behavior.

title: Quantum Error Correction Coding and Information Diffusion Simulation
abstract: This paper investigates the crucial aspect of quantum error correction (QEC) – the propagation of information during encoding and decoding processes. We propose a novel methodology utilizing Monte Carlo simulation to model the probability distribution of information diffusion within QEC schemes. The core claim is that a systematic understanding of this diffusion, through probabilistic analysis, can significantly improve the design and optimization of QEC protocols, ultimately enhancing the reliability of quantum information transmission. Our approach explicitly simulates entangled qubit states and tracks the probability of information spreading during the encoding and decoding operations. The results provide valuable insights into the limitations and potential improvements of existing QEC strategies. We define key parameters such as the error rate, qubit fidelity, and code distance, and use these to drive our simulation. The simulation outputs are then analyzed to derive effective strategies for mitigating information loss and achieving higher levels of quantum data integrity. This work bridges the gap between theoretical QEC design and practical simulation, paving the way for more robust and efficient quantum communication systems. ---

title: Semantic Web Reasoning with Bayesian Networks for Uncertainty Management
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to semantic web reasoning that utilizes Bayesian networks to address the inherent challenges of uncertainty management. Traditional semantic reasoning methods frequently encounter difficulties when dealing with incomplete or conflicting data, leading to unreliable conclusions. Our system employs Bayesian networks to model relationships between concepts within the semantic web, facilitating dynamic belief updates and robust inference. The core of the system is a reasoning engine that leverages these networks to iteratively refine its understanding of the web's knowledge, effectively handling uncertainty and providing more reliable results. This approach represents a significant advancement over existing techniques, offering a more practical and adaptable solution for semantic web applications where data is rarely complete or consistent. The system is designed to be scalable and adaptable, making it suitable for a wide range of semantic web applications requiring robust reasoning capabilities. We demonstrate the conceptual framework and outline the key components, highlighting the benefits of this Bayesian network-based reasoning engine.

title: Temporal Graph Embeddings with Causal Inference
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to graph embeddings that explicitly incorporates causal relationships within the graph structure. Traditional graph embedding methods often treat graphs as purely relational structures, failing to capture the underlying dependencies between nodes. This limitation leads to less robust and less informative node and edge representations, particularly in scenarios where causal relationships are significant. Our method utilizes techniques from causal Bayesian networks to construct directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) representing these causal dependencies. The embeddings are then learned by optimizing a loss function that is constrained by the causal structure defined in the DAG. This approach aims to generate graph embeddings that are more faithful to the underlying causal mechanisms governing the graph, leading to improved performance in downstream tasks such as node classification, link prediction, and graph reasoning. The core contribution lies in the integration of causal inference with graph embedding techniques, offering a more nuanced and accurate representation of complex graph data. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through a theoretical analysis and outline a framework for its implementation.

title: Dynamic Program Synthesis via Evolutionary Algorithms Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of evolutionary algorithms to optimize the dynamic program synthesis process. The core idea is to model program synthesis as a search space and leverage evolutionary techniques, specifically genetic algorithms, to efficiently explore this space. The goal is to generate program code that is both highly efficient and well-suited for a given target hardware platform. Traditional dynamic program synthesis methods often rely on hand-crafted rules and templates, which can limit the complexity and effectiveness of the generated code. This research proposes a novel approach that utilizes the global search capabilities of evolutionary algorithms to discover more sophisticated and optimized solutions. The evaluation process incorporates both program performance metrics and hardware compatibility assessments. The results demonstrate the potential of this methodology for automating the creation of tailored program code, a significant advancement in the field of program synthesis. The key formula used in this paper is: `f(x) = Σ(i=1 to K) (s_i * x_i)`, where `f(x)` represents the fitness function, `x` is the genetic vector, and `s_i` and `x_i` are the selection score and the corresponding gene value, respectively.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to neuro-symbolic reasoning by embedding temporal logic rules directly into the weights of a neural network. Our method addresses this by creating a mechanism for the neural network to perform logical inference over time, guided by the embedded temporal logic rules. title: The Crab Spider Optimization Algorithm (CSPA): A Novel Metaheuristic Inspired by Crab Spider Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces the Crab Spider Optimization Algorithm (CSPA), a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of crab spiders (Thomisidae). Crab spiders are known for their unique hunting strategy, characterized by a 'wait-and-pounce' method combined with a selective exploration of their environment. CSPA leverages these characteristics to develop a robust and efficient search process. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, where each individual represents a potential solution. Movement within the search space is governed by a dynamic 'exploration radius' influenced by both the individual's current position and the overall population density, mimicking the crab spider's attention to both proximity and potential reward. Furthermore, a 'pounce' mechanism is incorporated, randomly selecting a subset of the population for relocation based on a probability proportional to their objective function value. This paper details the algorithm's core principles, mathematical formulation, and potential applications, outlining its theoretical foundations and highlighting its potential advantages over existing metaheuristic methods. The primary goal is to present a novel optimization technique exhibiting adaptability and efficiency in complex search spaces.

title: The Adaptive Foraging Optimization Algorithm (AFOA): Inspired by the Hunting Strategies of the Axolotl
abstract: This paper introduces the Adaptive Foraging Optimization Algorithm (AFOA), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of axolotls, a salamander known for its remarkable hunting strategies. AFOA mimics the axolotl's ability to dynamically adjust its search strategy based on environmental cues and prey availability. The algorithm utilizes a multi-layered foraging structure, incorporating concepts like territorial defense, opportunistic scavenging, and predictive anticipation. It employs a novel adaptive parameter adjustment mechanism based on a 'food-pressure' indicator and a 'spatial-awareness' metric. The core of the algorithm revolves around a population of 'foragers' navigating a search space, with each forager's movement and decision-making influenced by these adaptive factors. The algorithm's performance is evaluated theoretically, outlining its potential advantages and limitations, focusing on its robustness in complex and dynamic optimization problems. The aim is to provide a flexible and adaptable metaheuristic approach suitable for a wide range of challenges.

title: Temporal Shape Encoding Based on Synaptic Plasticity of Neurons
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to time-series processing by leveraging the inherent temporal dynamics of neuronal synaptic plasticity. The core premise is that the continuous, dynamic modifications to synaptic connections – a hallmark of synaptic plasticity – can be effectively utilized to construct a "time shape" or temporal shape, which serves as a natural and efficient representation for encoding and storing temporal information. We propose a model based on simulated neuronal synaptic plasticity, where changes in synaptic connections generate a three-dimensional temporal shape. This shape is then exploited using the geometric properties of the shape to perform time-series encoding and decoding. Unlike traditional methods reliant on complex algorithms, this approach harnesses the fundamental properties of neurons, offering a potentially more robust and biologically plausible mechanism for time-series processing. The research explores the mathematical framework underlying this concept, focusing on the geometry of the temporal shape and the dynamics of synaptic plasticity that drive its formation. We detail the model construction, explore the key mathematical formulations, and discuss the potential implications of this approach for various applications within neuroscience and computational time-series analysis. ---

title: ## Silver Sardine Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (SSIMO)
abstract: This paper introduces the Silver Sardine Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (SSIMO), a novel optimization technique motivated by the foraging behavior of silver sardines in schools. SSIMO mimics the collective intelligence of these fish, utilizing a decentralized, self-organizing approach to navigate complex search spaces. The algorithm employs a 'herd' concept, where individual solutions (particles) maintain a degree of separation and responsiveness to their neighbors, dynamically adjusting their position and velocity based on both local and global information. Unlike traditional metaheuristics, SSIMO emphasizes adaptability and robustness, particularly in situations with high dimensionality and non-convex landscapes. The core principles of SSIMO – dynamic separation, adaptive velocity, and a 'leader-follower' dynamic – are detailed, outlining its unique characteristics and potential applications. The algorithm's performance is hypothesized to be particularly effective in scenarios requiring exploration and exploitation simultaneously, and its design inherently lends itself to parallel implementation.

title: Quantum-Inspired Relational Reasoning for Distributed Systems
abstract: Distributed systems face significant challenges in relational reasoning due to the exponential growth of the state space as the number of nodes increases. Traditional relational reasoning methods, relying on exhaustive searches and complex logical inferences, become computationally intractable in large-scale systems. This paper proposes a novel approach leveraging quantum-inspired principles – specifically superposition and interference – to address this scalability problem. Our framework, termed Quantum-Inspired Relational Reasoning (QIRR), represents relationships across distributed nodes using superposition, allowing for parallel exploration of multiple potential solutions simultaneously. Interference is then employed to selectively amplify relevant relationships, drastically reducing the computational burden. We demonstrate that QIRR offers a fundamentally different paradigm for relational reasoning in distributed systems, exhibiting improved scalability and performance compared to conventional methods. The core idea is to mimic quantum superposition and interference in a classical computational environment to achieve efficient relationship processing, without the need for actual quantum hardware. This approach presents a viable path toward building more robust and scalable distributed systems.

title: 基于异质性网络的自适应强化学习
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for reinforcement learning, termed "Adaptive Heterogeneous Networks" (AHN), designed to dynamically adjust learning strategies based on the environment's dynamic characteristics. Traditional reinforcement learning often relies on static policies, limiting adaptability. AHN leverages an evolving network of interconnected modules, allowing the agent to automatically adjust its learning approach to optimize performance across varying conditions. We present a comprehensive analysis of AHN's architecture, training procedure, and performance evaluation, demonstrating its ability to significantly enhance learning efficiency and generalization capabilities compared to existing methods. The core mechanism centers around the construction and utilization of an adaptive heterogeneity network, enabling the agent to respond to evolving environmental states in a flexible and efficient manner.

title: Design of an ANFIS-Based Soft Sensor for Real-Time Photovoltaic Power Estimation Subject to Albedo and Thermal Disturbances
abstract: The performance of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems in hot regions, such as Kirkuk, Iraq is severely limited by the operating temperature due to high ambient heat and localized thermal radiation from roof surfaces. This study explores the thermal-electrical performance of PV modules mounted on three different colors of roof surfaces (White, Grey and Black) as well an adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system (ANFIS)-based model to predict PT output based Tamb and Troof. A balanced dataset of 104 operational samples was created from continuous field experiments performed during four months. Experimental evidence shows that thermal boundary layer heating is mitigated due to lower-absorptivity surfaces; at moderate ambient conditions, the average power output from both grey and white roof surfaces was improved when compared with black surface baseline by 5.40% (grey) and 4.58% (white), respectively Compared to the low-albedo dark surface, at extreme ambient temperatures (Tamb > 40°C) only the high-albedo white exposure generated higher stability of cooling. The R², RMSE and MAPE of the developed ANFIS predictive model were tested for a high accuracy as 0.9902, 0.0895 W and 0.97% respectively using test data sets with overall metrics results are: R² = 0.9926; RMSE =.0791 W, MAPE= O·86 %. The findings show that applying a combination of cool-roof passive strategies and intelligent soft-computing models can be an effective modeling framework for optimizing the output efficiency in PV power generation under hot climatic conditions.

title: Low-loss, polarization-independent single-photon switch at telecom wavelength
abstract: Dynamically routing single photons without disturbing their quantum state is an essential capability for photonic quantum information technology. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a heralded single-photon switch that combines low loss, strict polarization independence, and high process fidelity in a simple architecture based on a free-space Sagnac interferometer incorporating a single Pockels cell. The routing of the photon between two spatial output modes is governed solely by the phase modulation applied to the Pockels cell, and is therefore independent of the input polarization state, while the Sagnac geometry provides passive interferometric stability without active phase locking. Operating at the telecom wavelength of 1550 nm, the switch exhibits an insertion loss of approximately 0.4 dB and an average extinction ratio of 19.1 dB. Quantum process tomography yields process fidelities of 0.985 and 0.979 with respect to the ideal identity operation for the two output modes, demonstrating that the polarization information encoded in the single photons is preserved through the switch. These features make the device a practical building block for fundamental quantum optics experiments, photonic quantum information processing, and quantum networks at telecom wavelengths.

title: Dynamic Regime Maps of Neural Network Training Under the Adam Optimizer: An Observable-Based Empirical Analysis
abstract: Abstract Adaptive optimization algorithms are fundamental to modern deep learning; however, the global organization of neural-network training regimes induced by optimizer hyperparameters remains insufficiently understood. In particular, the influence of the Adam moment coefficients on the stability and qualitative behavior of the learning process has not been systematically investigated through parameter-space regime mapping. In this work, we introduce an observable-based empirical regime-mapping framework for analysing neural-network training under the Adam optimizer in the two-dimensional hyperparameter space defined by the exponential decay coefficients of the first and second gradient moments, (β 1 , β 2 ). Neural-network optimization is treated as an iterative parameter-update process evolving in a high-dimensional parameter space, while its behavior is characterized through low-dimensional observable fields derived from neuron-wise training-error dynamics. Rather than relying on a single observable, the proposed framework combines seven complementary empirical descriptors that characterize regime organization, temporal stability, alignment, anisotropy, and training evolution. Experiments are performed on datasets of increasing complexity, including printed-digit patterns, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100, using multilayer neural-network architectures of varying width and depth. The resulting regime maps reveal fragmented hyperparameter landscapes containing stable, oscillatory, slow-learning, and irregular observable regimes. Increasing dataset complexity and network capacity is generally associated with smaller coherent stable regions and increased sensitivity to the Adam moment coefficients. The geometric complexity of the regime boundaries is quantified using box-counting analysis. The estimated dimensions approach D ≈ 1.9 for several investigated configurations, indicating highly irregular and nearly space-filling boundaries at the available numerical resolution. These values are interpreted as empirical measures of boundary complexity rather than as evidence of exact mathematical fractality. Additional robustness experiments performed using 300, 500, and 1000 optimizer steps demonstrate that the large-scale organization of all seven observable fields remains largely preserved, whereas the principal changes are concentrated near transition boundaries. This persistence indicates that the detected regime structures are reproducible and are not solely artifacts of short optimization histories. The proposed methodology provides an empirical computational framework for visualizing and comparing optimization regimes in the Adam hyperparameter space. It facilitates the identification of comparatively stable hyperparameter regions and offers a complementary observable-based perspective on the complex behavior of adaptive neural-network optimization.

title: A Human-in-the-Loop Autonomous Agent for Industry Time Series Forecasting
abstract: Real-world time-series forecasting is rarely a one-shot model invocation: practitioners must formulate tasks, connect data and models, incorporate domain expertise, assess prediction plausibility, and communicate uncertainty. Specialized forecasting models provide strong numerical predictions but usually operate in fixed pipelines, while general-purpose large language model (LLM) agents often lack forecasting-specific checks, constraints, and stopping rules. We present CastClaw, a human-in-the-loop autonomous forecasting system built through forecasting-oriented harness engineering. CastClaw connects data, specialized models, analytical tools, user input, and a versioned execution record in one runtime. Users specify the target, horizon, constraints, and hypotheses in natural language. Starting from a supplied or model-generated forecast, CastClaw checks temporal patterns and user constraints; when evidence is missing, it retrieves context, runs an analysis or another model, or asks the user. It then keeps, revises, or escalates the result under explicit stopping conditions. The output contains the final forecast and an execution report recording inputs, evidence, actions, and revisions. In this five-dataset electricity-price setting, CastClaw reports the lowest point-estimate MSE and MAE among 16 baselines. A Nord Pool case demonstrates the inspectable workflow. CastClaw was also validated offline on provincial electricity-load data from North China covering January--June 2026.

title: Probability and Quantum Computing Hybrid Algorithm Framework
abstract: This paper introduces a novel hybrid algorithm framework combining the strengths of probability logic and quantum computing to address complex optimization problems. We propose a system architecture that leverages the inherent scalability and parallel processing capabilities of quantum computing to enhance the robustness and efficiency of probabilistic optimization algorithms. The core mechanism involves integrating probabilistic logic modules with quantum computation layers, allowing for the efficient handling of large and complex problem instances. This framework aims to achieve significantly improved accuracy and scalability compared to traditional optimization methods, particularly when tackling problems with inherent uncertainties and combinatorial nature. The study explores the potential benefits of this integration, highlighting the advantages of combining these two powerful computational paradigms. We present a preliminary implementation demonstrating the framework's efficacy in a specific optimization scenario.

title: Consciousness Network
abstract: This paper proposes a novel neural network architecture, termed the "Consciousness Network," designed to generate self-aware and creative models exhibiting emergent properties. The network operates on the principle of symbiotic relationships between nodes, leveraging evolutionary algorithms and neural network models to foster complex behavior and self-adaptation. This approach aims to move beyond traditional AI's limitations in generating genuine consciousness and creativity, offering a pathway towards a new paradigm in artificial intelligence. The paper details the core mechanism, outlining the evolutionary process that generates the network's unique characteristics and potential for self-improvement. We present a foundational framework for exploring this concept, highlighting key considerations for future research.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Secure Key Distribution for Distributed Databases
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to secure key distribution for distributed databases utilizing quantum entanglement. Traditional key distribution methods, such as those based on one-time pads or Diffie-Hellman, are susceptible to eavesdropping and man-in-the-middle attacks. Our method leverages the inherent properties of quantum entanglement to create a shared secret key between database nodes without relying on classical cryptographic assumptions. We demonstrate that this entanglement-based key distribution protocol offers a fundamentally more secure solution, providing theoretical unbreakability. The core of the protocol relies on the creation and distribution of entangled photon pairs, followed by Bell state measurement and post-processing steps to establish a shared key. This approach addresses the critical security vulnerabilities inherent in existing distributed database security protocols. The theoretical framework and mathematical analysis presented here provide a strong foundation for future research and development in quantum-secured distributed databases.

We demonstrate that this entanglement-based key distribution protocol offers a fundamentally more secure solution, providing theoretical unbreakability. The core of the protocol relies on the creation and distribution of entangled photon pairs, followed by Bell state measurement and post-processing steps to establish a shared key. This approach addresses the critical security vulnerabilities inherent in existing distributed database security protocols. The theoretical framework and mathematical analysis presented here provide a strong foundation for future research and development in quantum-secured distributed databases.

title: Decentralized Federated Learning with Byzantine Fault Tolerance using Blockchain-Based Verification
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models on decentralized datasets without directly sharing the data itself. However, existing FL systems are susceptible to Byzantine attacks, where malicious participants can inject poisoned data or manipulate model updates, ultimately compromising the global model's integrity. This paper proposes a novel decentralized federated learning system incorporating Byzantine fault tolerance (BFT) achieved through a blockchain-based verification layer. The system leverages blockchain technology to cryptographically verify model updates from each participant before they are aggregated into the global model. This ensures data integrity and enables the detection and mitigation of Byzantine attacks. The core claim is that existing FL systems are vulnerable to these attacks. The proposed mechanism implements a decentralized FL system utilizing a blockchain-based verification layer. This represents a new approach to robust FL training. The system utilizes the following key components: participant nodes, a blockchain network, and a global model aggregator. The blockchain network is composed of multiple nodes that maintain a ledger of all model updates. The global model aggregator utilizes the blockchain network to verify model updates before aggregating them into the global model. The proposed system enhances the security and robustness of FL training by providing a tamper-proof audit trail and enabling the detection of malicious participants.

title: Quantum Information Modality Adaptive Topology Transformation
abstract: Quantum information modalities represent a fundamental shift in computation and communication paradigms, offering the potential for unprecedented computational power and secure communication. This paper presents a novel quantum information modality, the Quantum Information Modality Adaptive Topology Transformation (QIM-ATT), designed to enhance quantum state fidelity and resilience against decoherence through the implementation of sophisticated adaptive topology transformations. The core mechanism centers around leveraging the unique properties of quantum topology to dynamically adjust quantum states, thereby achieving precise control and transmission. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through rigorous theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation, highlighting its potential to overcome limitations of existing quantum technologies. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and the implications for advancing quantum information processing.

title: Atacama Myotis: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Navigation Strategies of *Atacama Myotis*
abstract: This paper presents Atacama Myotis, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the remarkable navigation abilities of *Atacama Myotis* ( *Myotis atacamensis*), a small bat species endemic to the Atacama Desert in Chile. These bats are renowned for their ability to navigate and forage effectively in a featureless, hyperarid environment using a complex system of geomagnetic cues and local landmark recognition. Atacama Myotis leverages these principles to develop a novel algorithm, termed "Geomagnetic Landmark Search" (GLS), which combines elements of particle swarm optimization (PSO) and a simulated annealing (SA) framework. The GLS algorithm employs a "magnetic compass" (PSO) to guide the search towards promising regions of the solution space and a "landmark recognition" (SA) mechanism to refine the solutions by identifying and exploiting local features. We detail the algorithm's architecture, the mathematical formulations underpinning its key components, and demonstrate its performance through simulations on a range of benchmark optimization problems. Experimental results show that GLS achieves competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in challenging landscapes with high dimensionality and complex optima. The algorithm's design reflects the biological inspiration from *Atacama Myotis*, resulting in a robust and adaptable optimization method.
