title: Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning via Differentially Private Model Training
abstract: This paper explores the application of differential privacy (DP) to machine learning model training. Traditional machine learning relies on direct access to sensitive training data, posing significant privacy risks. We introduce a novel approach that integrates DP mechanisms into the model training process, mitigating these risks while maintaining model accuracy. The core idea involves adding calibrated noise during model parameter updates, effectively limiting the influence of any single data point on the final model. We examine the trade-offs between privacy and utility, demonstrating how adjusting the privacy parameter (ε) impacts model performance. Our framework offers a practical means of building machine learning models that respect data privacy, crucial for applications involving sensitive datasets such as healthcare and finance. The presented methodology provides a foundation for further research into adaptive DP strategies and robust model training within privacy constraints.

title: Relational Reinforcement Learning with Semantic Memory
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to relational reinforcement learning (RL) that integrates a semantic memory component. Existing relational RL methods often struggle with generalization, failing to adapt effectively to new environments. Our proposed system addresses this limitation by explicitly storing and retrieving relational knowledge within a semantic memory module. This allows the agent to leverage previously learned relationships to guide exploration and decision-making in unfamiliar scenarios. We demonstrate that this integration significantly enhances generalization capabilities, leading to improved performance across a range of environments. The core of the method lies in the dynamic updating and querying of this memory, enabling the agent to build a robust representation of the world and its relationships. The system's architecture includes an RL agent, a memory module storing relational facts, and a mechanism for retrieving and utilizing this knowledge. The key contribution of this work is the explicit incorporation of semantic memory within the relational RL framework, providing a pathway to more robust and adaptive learning.

title: Fractal Topology as a Computational Paradigm
abstract: Fractal topology, a burgeoning field of mathematics and computer science, presents a compelling computational paradigm for tackling complex optimization challenges. This paper explores the potential of fractal geometry as a foundational tool for algorithmic design, highlighting its capacity to generate self-similar structures that offer novel solutions for diverse problems. We argue that the inherent properties of fractal patterns—self-similarity, recursion, and sensitivity to initial conditions—provide a distinct advantage over conventional approaches in optimization, and that its application can unlock new avenues for computational problem-solving. title: Quantum Hiding Multi-Body Computation via Topological Structures
abstract: Quantum hiding multi-body computation is a burgeoning field that leverages the unique properties of quantum systems to simulate complex quantum phenomena. This paper presents a novel optimization algorithm, termed "Topological Optimization for Quantum Hiding," based on topological structure optimization. The core idea is to dynamically adjust the quantum system's state, guided by a carefully designed topological structure, to enhance computational efficiency and precision, particularly within the simulation of intricate quantum systems. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through comprehensive simulations and analysis, showcasing significant improvements in both computational speed and solution quality compared to existing methods. The algorithm's effectiveness stems from its ability to proactively shape the system's state, minimizing redundant calculations and facilitating the exploration of complex quantum configurations. The paper concludes with a discussion of the algorithm's potential applications across various quantum simulations and outlines future research directions.

title: Hyperparameter Optimization with Bayesian Optimization and Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to hyperparameter optimization that leverages the strengths of both Bayesian Optimization (BO) and Reinforcement Learning (RL). Traditional Bayesian Optimization often struggles with exploring complex hyperparameter spaces efficiently, frequently falling into local optima. Reinforcement Learning offers a dynamic strategy for adapting exploration, but integrating it seamlessly with BO remains a challenge. This work proposes an agent-based reinforcement learning framework where an RL agent learns to dynamically adjust the exploration parameters of a BO algorithm. The agent's objective is to maximize the performance of the BO search, effectively guiding it towards optimal hyperparameter configurations. The core claim of this research is that this combined approach significantly improves hyperparameter optimization. We define the problem as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) and formulate the agent's policy using a deep neural network. Experimental results, while not involving experimental validation, demonstrate the potential of this method. The key advancements lie in the adaptive exploration strategy and the dynamic adjustment of BO's exploration parameters. Further research can explore different RL algorithms and network architectures to enhance the optimization process.

abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, holds immense potential for technological advancement. This research explores the application of multi-dimensional space quantum entanglement to enhance the stability and scalability of quantum information transfer. The core of this investigation centers on the design of a quantum entanglement network operating within a multi-dimensional space, leveraging its unique properties to facilitate more robust and extended entanglement generation. This study will detail the theoretical foundations, experimental design, and preliminary results demonstrating the potential of this approach to revolutionize quantum information processing. The research will culminate in a comprehensive analysis of the framework's performance and potential applications, highlighting its advantages over existing methods.

title: ## Bamboo Beetle Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces the "Chrysomela" algorithm, a novel metaheuristic optimization technique inspired by the foraging behavior of bamboo beetles ( *Chrysomela* species). These insects exhibit a remarkable ability to efficiently locate and exploit food sources in complex and dynamic environments. The algorithm leverages the beetle's exploratory and exploitative strategies, combined with a novel concept of "resource density gradients" to guide the search process. The core mechanism involves a population of "scout beetles" that explore the search space, while "forager beetles" converge towards promising regions based on an adaptive evaluation function that incorporates both resource availability and gradient information. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and potential applications, highlighting its suitability for problems characterized by high dimensionality, non-linearity, and potentially sparse solutions. The algorithm's performance is expected to be particularly effective in scenarios where traditional optimization methods struggle due to the complexity of the search landscape.

title: Andersen's Bare-backed Fruit Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Fruit Bat Search" (FBS), inspired by the foraging behavior of Andersen's bare-backed fruit bats ( *Pteropus*). These bats exhibit a unique and highly efficient search strategy for locating fruit, utilizing a combination of exploration and exploitation. FBS leverages this behavior to develop an optimization algorithm suitable for a wide range of complex problems. The algorithm employs a position representation, a velocity vector, and a memory mechanism to simulate the bats' search process. The core innovation lies in the adaptive adjustment of the search probability based on the bat's position relative to the best-known solution, mimicking the bats' tendency to converge towards promising areas. The algorithm's performance is evaluated across several benchmark functions, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The key parameters of FBS, including the exploration factor (α) and the exploitation factor (β), are discussed in detail, and their influence on the algorithm's convergence and performance is analyzed. This paper provides a comprehensive description of FBS, its theoretical underpinnings, and its practical applications.

title: # Anaguma: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Anaguma
abstract: This paper presents Anaguma, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Anaguma, a unique insect found in the Amazon rainforest. The Anaguma exhibits a remarkable ability to locate food sources within complex and dynamic environments. Anaguma leverages this behavior by employing a novel exploration and exploitation strategy based on probabilistic movement and local search. The algorithm incorporates a dynamic food source model, simulating the Anaguma's search process, and utilizes a weighted sum approach for solution evaluation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Anaguma through simulations on benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The key contributions of this work lie in the algorithm's unique search mechanism and its potential application in solving various complex optimization problems. The algorithm's performance is evaluated using metrics such as convergence rate, solution accuracy, and computational efficiency. Experimental results indicate that Anaguma offers a promising alternative for tackling challenging optimization tasks.

title: Quantum Topology Network Learning Algorithm (QTLA)
abstract: Quantum topology networks (QTN) represent a novel framework for quantum computation, offering unique computational capabilities and potential for advanced quantum algorithms. Traditional approaches to learning and optimizing these networks often rely on static parameters, limiting their adaptability. This paper introduces the Quantum Topology Network Learning Algorithm (QTLA), a novel algorithm designed to learn and optimize the topological structure of QTNs, thereby enhancing the performance of quantum computation. We present a mechanism leveraging the inherent topological properties of QTNs as learning objectives, employing a quantum algorithm to automatically refine the network's structure and achieve optimal performance. The development of QTLA addresses limitations in existing methods by providing a dynamic and adaptable approach to network optimization.

title: Contextual Reinforcement Learning with Bayesian Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to reinforcement learning (RL) that leverages Bayesian networks to effectively handle contextual information. Traditional RL algorithms often struggle in complex environments where the optimal policy depends heavily on the current state and relevant contextual factors. This work introduces a framework where a Bayesian network explicitly models the relationships between the agent's state (s), the environment's state (e), and the expected reward (r). The agent employs this network to perform Bayesian inference, updating its policy (π) and making decisions based on probabilistic reasoning. The core benefit lies in the network's ability to represent dependencies and uncertainties, leading to more robust and interpretable policies compared to purely deterministic RL methods. We demonstrate, through theoretical analysis and a simplified illustrative example, the potential for this approach to significantly improve performance in environments with complex, dynamic relationships. The key innovation is the integration of Bayesian inference into the learning process, providing a mechanism for the agent to reason about the potential impact of different actions given the current context. The framework offers a path toward creating more adaptable and reliable RL agents.

title: AI-Driven Topic Modeling and Sentiment Analysis of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Discussions on Social Media: Cross-Platform Study
abstract: Background: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a multifactorial autoimmune disease influenced by genetic, epigenetic, ecological, and environmental factors, with a global prevalence of 7.7 to 13 per 100,000, and standardized mortality rates of 2.4% to 5.9%. Between 14% and 75% of patients experience psychiatric comorbidities such as anxiety and depression, which impair treatment adherence and health-related quality of life. Social media has become an important channel for patients to express health concerns and seek support. Reddit and Weibo, as mainstream platforms globally and in China, respectively, host large volumes of user-generated content; however, no prior study has examined SLE-related discourse across both cultural and platform contexts. Objective: This study aimed to characterize SLE-related discussions on Reddit and Weibo. Specifically, we sought to identify and hierarchically categorize discussion topics, compare platform-specific differences in patient concerns, assess sentiment polarity across topics and thematic groups, and characterize public misconceptions related to SLE. Methods: This observational, computational content analysis examined all SLE-related discussions on Reddit (r/lupus) and Weibo up to November 30, 2024. An AI-driven pipeline first embedded the discussions using the Multilingual-E5-base BERT (bidirectional encoder representations from transformers) model, then applied uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) for dimensionality reduction and hierarchical density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise (HDBSCAN) for density-based clustering to identify fine-grained topics, with keywords extracted via class-based term frequency-inverse document frequency (c-TF-IDF). Topics were further grouped into higher-level thematic domains through spectral clustering, with labels and definitions generated using GPT-5 Thinking via prompt engineering. Sentiment polarity (positive, neutral, and negative) was classified using a fine-tuned multilingual BERT model. Two clinical pharmacists independently validated the topic modeling and sentiment results. Results: We analyzed 11,318 discussions from 3649 unique authors on Reddit and 33,628 discussions from 21,509 authors on Weibo. We identified 99 fine-grained topics on Reddit and 189 on Weibo, grouped into 6 thematic domains per platform. Reddit discussions centered on diagnostic journeys, treatment experiences, and symptom management, whereas Weibo discussions emphasized social news, charitable activities, and traditional Chinese medicine (eg, artemisinin). The overall sentiment on Reddit was positive (mean 0.42, SD 0.86; 95% CI 0.40-0.43), whereas that on Weibo was neutral (mean 0.01, SD 0.91; 95% CI 0.00-0.02). Sentiment was positive in 7493, neutral in 1032, and negative in 2793 Reddit discussions, whereas on Weibo, it was positive, neutral, and negative in 14,026, 5768, and 13,834 discussions, respectively. Treatment-related misconceptions and unverified remedies recurred on both platforms. Conclusions: This cross-platform analysis reveals both shared and platform-specific concerns among people with SLE, highlighting distinct informational and emotional needs across cultural and platform contexts. Recurring treatment-related misconceptions and the substantial volume of negative-sentiment discussions warrant targeted public health communication and psychological support. The findings may help clinicians, public health authorities, and patient support organizations identify unmet needs, while the AI-driven approach offers a scalable, real-time tool for monitoring patient perspectives.

title: Vocal Music under Phoneme-Conditional Analysis
abstract: The vocal music of each language carries a distinctive sonic identity, even without instrumental accompaniment. We ask whether these differences are measurable and traceable to specific phonemes. To tackle this question, we introduce phoneme-conditional analysis, which isolates the acoustic effect of typologically distinctive phonemes by comparing marker syllables against matched non-marker controls within the same song, holding singer, melody, and genre constant. Across nine typologically diverse languages and thousands of songs, we measure effects along five acoustic dimensions. Song-level profiles built from these effects identify the language of an unaccompanied vocal at 85.5% balanced accuracy in a nine-way classification with folds grouped by artist; whether the separability arises by accumulation of the phoneme-local effects themselves is left open. Our findings suggest that phonological structure leaves systematic and measurable traces in how each language is sung.

title: Support Measurements for Identity-Fragmented Gradient Evaluation
abstract: Direct measurements are reported for the causal support of initialization gradients in identity-fragmented variational circuits. Evaluation restricted to the computed causal support reproduces full-register simulation to 1.4 × 10^−16, and gradients for parameters whose support excludes the observable vanish to 2.75×10^−17 rather than merely becoming small. Support cardinality is min(N, 4ℓ) on nearest-neighbour connectivity and min(N, 8ℓ) with an added antipodal coupling, where ℓ is prefix depth and N the register size, and is independent of N once the register exceeds the support. For a local observable at fixed fragment depth K, the number of parameters surviving the support criterion is 2K^2 −2K +1 on the nearest-neighbour topology, also independent of N . A stacked-block control separates nominal circuit depth from effective causal depth: a 256-amplitude prefix tile reproduces a circuit of 96 macro-layers to 2.1 × 10^−16, while the corresponding cone of a plain circuit grows linearly in depth. Controls establish the limits of the construction, including failure of tile reuse under general input states. Two corrections to the support bound and the tile-count figure of the replication manuscript are reported. A finer object is then measured: the set of gate transitions, rather than qubits, on which the answer depends. At N = 14 and prefix depth 2, eighteen of fifty-six gates suffice. All figures are reproducible from the accompanying scripts.

evidence.abstract: Direct measurements are reported for the causal support of initialization gradients in identity-fragmented variational circuits. This repository formally verifies, in Lean 4, several foundational structures of differential equations and dynamical systems — the evolution of ODEs, integral transforms, iteration of dynamical systems, convergence of Picard iteration, and fixed points of linear systems — observing a preliminary phenomenon: the action residual ε does not break topological properties such as convergence and stability, but it does break algebraic structures such as linearity. ——老陈与AI的深夜实验室 发布 请笑纳—— — Published by Lao Chen & AI's Late Night Lab. title: 基于高阶矩阵的动态量子态的量子计算
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum computing approach based on dynamic quantum states, leveraging the self-adaptive properties of high-rank matrices. We propose a quantum computing framework that utilizes the inherent ability of high-rank matrices to dynamically adjust quantum states, thereby enhancing the efficiency and precision of quantum computations. This design focuses on mitigating the limitations of traditional quantum algorithms and opens possibilities for more complex and robust quantum systems. The core mechanism involves constructing a quantum computing framework that adapts to the state, enabling efficient and accurate quantum processing. This paper explores the advantages and potential challenges of this approach, emphasizing the role of high-rank matrices in driving quantum performance.

title: Title: Universal Quantum State Representation for Pattern Recognition
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to pattern recognition utilizing a quantum state representation capable of encoding any pattern, including complex symbolic and visual information. Current methods largely rely on data-driven techniques, limiting the potential for truly transformative pattern recognition. We introduce a new representation – the "Quantum State Encoding" – that leverages the inherent properties of quantum mechanics to encode patterns directly within the quantum state itself. This approach promises a paradigm shift in pattern recognition, potentially surpassing the capabilities of existing algorithms by offering a level of abstraction and interpretability not currently available. The core mechanism focuses on dynamically evolving the quantum state to represent patterns, eliminating the need for explicit feature engineering and enabling robust pattern identification across diverse data types. We explore the mathematical framework underpinning this approach and provide a preliminary demonstration of its capabilities through a simplified example.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Temporal Logic Programming
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for temporal reasoning that integrates the capabilities of neural networks and symbolic temporal logic. The core idea is to leverage the pattern recognition strengths of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) alongside the precise reasoning abilities of temporal logic. We introduce a system where an RNN learns temporal patterns from input data, and a temporal logic engine utilizes these learned patterns to generate and execute logical rules. This neuro-symbolic approach aims to overcome the limitations of traditional methods – purely neural networks often lack explainability and robustness, while purely symbolic systems struggle with complex, noisy data. The system presented here offers a more robust and explainable solution by combining the inductive learning of neural networks with the deductive reasoning of temporal logic, leading to improved accuracy and transparency in temporal reasoning tasks. The system is designed for scenarios where temporal dependencies are crucial, such as robotics, autonomous driving, and process monitoring, where both accurate pattern detection and logical consistency are paramount.

title: ##基于图神经网络的复杂系统建模
abstract: This paper explores the application of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for modeling complex systems. Complex systems, such as social networks and biological networks, are characterized by intricate interdependencies and emergent behaviors. Traditional modeling approaches often struggle to capture these complexities effectively. GNNs offer a powerful alternative by leveraging the inherent structure of complex systems, represented as graphs. This work details the core claim of utilizing GNNs to reveal underlying system structures and dynamics. The central mechanism involves constructing systems as nodes and edges within a graph and employing GNNs for tasks like node classification, relationship prediction, and graph embedding learning. We argue that this approach represents a significant expansion of GNNs' applicability, providing a novel method for understanding and analyzing complex systems. The research focuses on theoretical foundations and conceptual development, without necessitating experimental validation. ---

title: Title: Cognitive Resonance Mapping (CRM)
abstract: Cognitive Resonance Mapping (CRM) is a novel computational method designed to quantitatively analyze and predict the 'cognitive resonance' of neural networks – the patterns of activation and feedback that drive learning. This method leverages a generative adversarial network (GAN) to iteratively refine a neural network's representation, optimizing for a specific 'resonance' metric that correlates with task performance. Current AI systems primarily rely on supervised learning, creating a significant gap in our ability to understand and control the cognitive processes underlying learning. CRM offers a pathway towards self-calibration and predictive modeling, potentially unlocking more efficient and robust AI systems.

title: Black Spider Monkey Algorithm: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Black Spider Monkey Behavior
abstract: This paper proposes a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm, the Black Spider Monkey Algorithm (BSMA), inspired by the foraging and social behavior of black spider monkeys. BSMA leverages the monkey's unique ability to climb trees, exploit food sources, and communicate effectively to create a novel search strategy. The algorithm utilizes a combination of adaptive step size adjustment, a novel population diversity maintenance mechanism mimicking monkey social dynamics, and a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance. The core of BSMA involves a simulated climbing motion, a food source representation, and a communication network to guide the search process. The performance of BSMA is evaluated through a series of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results highlight the potential of BSMA as a robust and adaptable optimization tool for various complex problems. The algorithm's key parameters are designed to enhance its convergence speed and solution quality. The evaluation focuses on demonstrating BSMA's capability to find near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time.

title: Quantum States and the Evolution of Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum state transformations as a novel approach to quantum computing. Traditional quantum computation often relies on static, pre-defined quantum states, limiting the scope of computational possibilities. We propose a design of a non-linear transformation algorithm driven by quantum state dynamics, leveraging quantum computing's inherent properties to achieve precise computations and modeling. The core mechanism focuses on manipulating the quantum state through non-linear transformations to generate a precise solution. This research aims to address the limitations of current quantum algorithms by offering a fundamentally different approach to state evolution and computation.

title: ##混沌映射的量子加速算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to chaos mapping employing quantum entanglement to accelerate the evolution and analysis of chaotic systems. The core mechanism focuses on leveraging quantum entanglement to significantly reduce computational cost and enhance prediction accuracy, offering a potentially transformative tool for studying complex dynamical systems. We detail the algorithm's design, its potential advantages over traditional methods, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its efficacy in accelerating and predicting chaotic behavior. This work represents a significant step towards harnessing the power of quantum mechanics for enhanced chaos analysis.

title: Adaptive Neuron Topology Networks for Generation
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural network architecture design utilizing adaptive neuron topology networks (ANTNs). The core idea revolves around mimicking the self-organizing properties observed in biological neural networks to autonomously generate networks with desired functionality and performance. We employ an evolutionary algorithm to dynamically adjust the connection strength and type between network nodes, driven by simulated neuron behavior and feedback mechanisms. This process allows for an adaptive network topology, overcoming the limitations of traditional, manually-designed neural networks. The system's capacity to evolve autonomously represents a significant advancement in neural network design, offering a potentially more efficient and effective method for creating specialized architectures. The key innovation lies in the integration of neuron simulation and evolutionary optimization to achieve truly self-generated networks. The resulting networks are evaluated based on their ability to perform specific tasks, demonstrating the potential of ANTs for a wide range of applications.

title: Adaptive Lattice-Based Probability Theory (ALPT)
abstract: This paper presents Adaptive Lattice-Based Probability Theory (ALPT), a novel probabilistic framework centered on dynamically evolving lattice structures. We explore a system designed to quantify uncertainty at the micro-level, offering a pathway beyond traditional probability theory's static representations. The core innovation lies in the iterative refinement of a lattice through simulations, incorporating adaptive rules that dynamically adjust the probability distribution based on environmental factors. This system aims to provide a more nuanced and robust understanding of uncertainty, particularly in complex and evolving systems. The paper details the design of the lattice, the iterative refinement process, and preliminary results demonstrating the framework's potential for handling intricate environments.

title: Algorithmic Transparency via Formal Specification and Verification of Machine Learning Pipelines
abstract: The increasing deployment of machine learning (ML) models across various domains raises significant concerns regarding trust, accountability, and understanding. Many ML models operate as "black boxes," making it difficult to comprehend their decision-making processes and identify potential biases or errors. This research addresses this challenge by proposing a framework for formally specifying and verifying the entire machine learning pipeline. The framework leverages formal specification languages and automated verification tools to guarantee that the pipeline adheres to predefined requirements and behaves consistently. This approach moves beyond post-hoc explanations, providing a rigorous and verifiable foundation for trust in ML systems. The core contribution lies in the systematic application of formal methods to the complete ML pipeline, offering a novel mechanism for achieving algorithmic transparency. We define key metrics and utilize mathematical formalisms to represent the pipeline's behavior, allowing for automated checks against intended functionality. The overall goal is to enable developers and stakeholders to confidently deploy and utilize ML models, knowing that their operation is demonstrably sound and aligned with ethical and regulatory standards.

title: ##拓扑量子纠缠的自适应优化算法
abstract: Quantum entanglement offers unprecedented opportunities for quantum computation and communication, but its practical implementation often faces limitations due to the difficulty of controlling quantum states. This paper explores the potential of leveraging quantum entanglement to develop a novel self-adaptive optimization algorithm for quantum systems. We propose a "quantum state graph" concept, where quantum bits are represented as nodes and entanglement properties are used to dynamically adjust qubit arrangements. This approach aims to overcome the inherent challenges of controlling quantum systems through classical optimization methods, potentially unlocking new capabilities in quantum information processing. The core mechanism involves utilizing pulse-based control to manipulate entanglement and achieve precise results. This research introduces a framework for dynamically adapting quantum states, offering a pathway toward more efficient and robust quantum algorithms.

title: Based on Quantum Error Correction Codes: A Distributed Storage System
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed storage system design utilizing quantum error correction (QEC) codes. The core claim is that incorporating QEC allows for robust data redundancy within a distributed system, significantly enhancing data reliability and security against various forms of noise and corruption. The proposed mechanism involves encoding data using selected QEC codes before distribution across the network, effectively mitigating the impact of quantum noise. This work outlines the fundamental principles, key considerations, and potential challenges associated with implementing such a system. Specifically, we explore different QEC codes and their suitability for distributed storage, discuss the overhead associated with encoding and decoding, and address scalability concerns. The research presents a theoretical framework for a QEC-based distributed storage system, demonstrating the potential for significantly improved data preservation compared to traditional redundancy schemes. The system's architecture emphasizes efficient data distribution and retrieval while maintaining the integrity of encoded data. This approach offers a pathway toward building highly resilient storage solutions for applications demanding high data availability and security, particularly in quantum computing environments.

title: Quantum Entanglement Transfer for Topological Error Correction
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum error correction leveraging the topological properties of quantum entanglement. Traditional quantum error correction codes rely on local operations, which are often inefficient and vulnerable to noise. We propose a scheme utilizing multi-body quantum entanglement networks to encode and decode quantum information, capitalizing on the inherent topological protection offered by entanglement. The core mechanism involves the exchange of entangled states to effectively mitigate the impact of noise, achieving robust quantum information transfer without the constraints of localized operations. This work introduces a fundamentally new paradigm for quantum communication, offering a more reliable pathway for transmitting quantum information in the presence of environmental noise. The proposed method aims to overcome the limitations of existing error correction techniques by exploiting the intrinsic robustness of entanglement, paving the way for more practical and scalable quantum communication systems. The key advantage lies in the absence of the need for local quantum gates, which are often a significant bottleneck in quantum communication. We demonstrate, theoretically, the potential for enhanced error correction performance through the strategic manipulation of entangled states.

title: Ambon Flying Fox: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Flight Dynamics of a Flying Fox
abstract: This paper introduces Ambon Flying Fox (AFF), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the flight dynamics of the Ambon flying fox ( *Pteropus motschleri*). The algorithm leverages the animal's unique aerial maneuvering capabilities, specifically its ability to rapidly change direction and altitude, to develop a robust and efficient optimization strategy. AFF combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC), incorporating a dynamic velocity update mechanism and a novel convergence control strategy mimicking the flying fox's flight pattern. The algorithm's core innovation lies in its adaptive velocity adjustment, which is influenced by both the particle's search experience and a simulated environmental gradient. We demonstrate AFF's effectiveness through simulations on benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to outperform traditional metaheuristics in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. The key mathematical formulations and algorithmic steps are presented, providing a clear and detailed description of AFF's implementation. The algorithm's performance is evaluated using metrics such as convergence rate, solution accuracy, and computational complexity. The results indicate that AFF presents a promising alternative for tackling complex optimization challenges across diverse domains.

title: ## Altai Vole: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of the Altai Vole
abstract: This paper presents Altai Vole, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging strategies of the Altai vole, a small rodent known for its efficient and adaptive movement patterns in complex, multi-dimensional landscapes. The algorithm leverages the vole's observed behaviors – particularly its tendency to explore areas with high resource density while simultaneously exploiting previously visited areas – to create a robust and effective optimization process. Altai Vole incorporates elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) within a dynamically adjusting exploration-exploitation framework. The algorithm's core mechanism involves a 'resource density' metric, calculated based on the historical search space coverage, to guide particle movement. The parameters influencing the balance between exploration and exploitation are dynamically adjusted based on the perceived stagnation of the search. Performance evaluations on a range of benchmark optimization problems demonstrate that Altai Vole exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in problems with high dimensionality and complex landscapes. The key contributions of this work lie in the innovative application of animal behavior as a source of inspiration for metaheuristic design and the development of a dynamically adaptive exploration-exploitation strategy.

title: Non-Linear Geometry Structures: Probability Field Expansion
abstract: This paper investigates the application of non-linear geometry structures to probability field expansion, aiming to overcome the limitations of traditional probabilistic modeling. We propose a novel framework that dynamically adjusts geometric parameters to simulate the evolution of system states, offering a more accurate representation of complex geometric systems. The core mechanism centers around the integration of a geometric structure that governs the system's state dynamics, enabling precise prediction and modeling of dynamic behavior. This work represents a significant advancement in probabilistic modeling, particularly for systems exhibiting intricate geometric properties. The theoretical foundations and experimental validation of this approach will be presented, demonstrating the potential for enhanced predictive capabilities.

title: Paper UAP-I Cross-Flight Shared-Latent-State Validation on Independent Radar and Passive RF Sensing of a Known UAV A Positive-Control Governance Benchmark Before Multi-Sensor UAP Application
abstract: This paper tests a shared latent state method on a known physical target before applying the method to unidentified anomalous phenomena. Public AERPAW data provide independent Fortem radar measurements, Keysight passive radio frequency localization estimates, and ground truth unmanned aerial vehicle telemetry. Optimal Flight 2 is used for calibration and protocol development, while Optimal Flights 1 and 3 are used for cross flight validation. The published radar orientation correction is retained rather than adjusted separately for each validation flight. The analysis compares independent radar and radio frequency state models with a single causal state updated by both sensors, with every observation scored before it is used to update the model. On Optimal Flight 1, the shared state improves radio frequency prediction by about sixty five percent while radar prediction worsens by about six percent, producing an overall predictive improvement of about thirty nine percent. On Optimal Flight 3, radio frequency prediction improves by about seventy four percent, radar prediction worsens by about six percent, and the overall predictive improvement is about forty eight percent. Dependence aware time block resampling supports the improvement on both flights. A separate localization test does not show an advantage for fusion because radar alone remains slightly more accurate than the shared state. The results therefore support shared state predictive transfer between independent sensors observing one known object, but do not support improved localization beyond the strongest sensor. The experiment is a positive control validation of the methodology and does not provide evidence for unidentified anomalous phenomena, Holosphere physics, or any nonordinary mechanism.

title: The influence of cultural lag on integrating artificial intelligence in software development
abstract: Background: Material culture evolves faster than non-material culture when new technologies emerge, creating a cultural lag that misaligns society, hinders artificial intelligence (AI) integration, and causes resistance, potentially leading to failed integration efforts. Objectives: The study applies Ogburn’s theory to the modern context of AI, identifying material and non-material cultures that influence its integration and proposing strategies to reduce cultural lag. Method: The research is grounded in an interpretivist worldview, employing an inductive, qualitative approach rooted in phenomenology. Semi-structured interviews served as the primary data collection method, and thematic analysis supported by ATLAS.ti provided a systematic approach to analysing the data. Results: The findings revealed that the company’s material culture reflects a multi-tool AI environment. However, non-material cultures (infrastructure limitations, operational constraints, subscription costs, and procurement choices) created a cultural lag. Strategies to reduce this lag were proposed, including leadership communication, structured enablement and operational improvements. Conclusion: This study established the need to explore material and non-material cultures influencing AI integration and to develop strategies to reduce cultural lag. While AI can transform industries, resistance because of cultural lag often hinders integration, underscoring the need to understand these cultures. Contribution: The study contributes a strategy model that can assist software development companies and other industries in addressing the gap between technological innovation and cultural adaptation. The findings seek to benefit software developers, IT professionals, business leaders and academics by facilitating smoother technological transitions and improving AI implementation in the industry.

title: Toward a Causally-Inspired Evolving World Model for Vision-and-Language Navigation in Continuous Environments
abstract: Vision-and-Language Navigation in Continuous Environments (VLN-CE) has emerged as a pivotal challenge in Embodied AI, requiring an agent to navigate 3D spaces guided by natural language instructions. Drawing inspiration from human cognition, world models provide a powerful paradigm by predicting environment dynamics and enabling reasoning beyond immediate observations. However, existing world model-based VLN methods remain static once trained - their representations rely on fixed correlation-based priors rather than adaptive causal structures, making them unable to accommodate evolving confounders and changing observation-action dependencies across environments. This rigidity leads to overfitting to training-specific patterns and degraded performance under distribution shifts. To address this limitation, we propose a causally-inspired evolving world modeling framework that formulates VLN-CE as a sequence of causal partially observable Markov decision processes. Our model learns unified latent states that integrate vision, language, and action, while addressing spurious correlations through a dual-level intervention mechanism: at the observation level, frequency-domain perturbations simulate superficial appearance variations to enhance perceptual robustness; at the representation level, cross-episode confounder buffers perform counterfactual substitution to approximate the influence of latent confounding factors. Beyond static world modeling, our framework continuously evolves, refining these proxy representations across episodes, enabling efficient adaptation to previously unseen environments. Building on this evolving causally-inspired foundation, our world model supports counterfactual reasoning and strengthens generalization across diverse navigation contexts. Extensive evaluations on established VLN-CE benchmarks demonstrate that our method outperforms existing approaches, delivering superior navigation performance across diverse scenarios. Real-world robot evaluations further validate the practicality of our approach. Code is available in the Supplementary Material.

title: Lucida: Parse, Generate, and Place for Composable Real-to-Sim Scene Modeling
abstract: Composable scene modeling aims to recover a real indoor scene as complete, editable object assets arranged as observed, giving robot simulation and embodied AI a simulation-ready replica of the real environment whose objects can be manipulated individually. Existing pipelines decompose the task into three steps---parse the observations into instances, generate an asset for each, and place each asset back---but every step presumes an input that a cluttered capture rarely provides: accurate instance geometry, unoccluded views, and assets that accurately match the observations. We propose Lucida, which keeps this order but redistributes the requirements, so each step consumes only what a real capture reliably provides and precision is reached at the end of the pipeline rather than demanded at its start. Lucida parses the video into a scene graph whose nodes carry per-instance multi-view evidence, generates a complete asset for each instance from its evidence, and places assets with GizmoAct, a VLM policy that casts placement as multi-turn GUI interaction, manipulating the object's gizmo in a closed loop and deciding itself when alignment is reached. Across scene-level 3D object detection, object pose estimation, and scene reconstruction, Lucida improves mAP over Boxer by 69% on R2S-Scene, raises ADD-SB@0.05 from 57.8% to 83.4% on CA-1M, and increases scene F-Score from 0.794 for SAM3D to 0.924.

title: Toolkit for Measuring Contextual Individuation in Transformer Language Models
abstract: First stable release, archived for citation and auditing alongside its companion manuscript, Technical Manual for a Toolkit for Measuring Contextual Individuation in Transformer Language Models. Contents contextual_individuation.ipynb — the full pipeline: bridge-form declaration, Wikipedia corpus acquisition, occurrence localization, layer-wise representation extraction, pairwise silhouette measurement, and paired PCA visualization. requirements.txt — pinned dependency versions for local reproducibility. .env.example — template for the contact-email variable used in the Wikipedia API User-Agent header. License CC BY 4.0 — free to use, share, and adapt, including for auditing this tool against the paper it accompanies, with attribution. Citation Please cite this archived release (not the manuscript alone) when reporting results produced with the toolkit; cite the companion manuscript when referring to its design rationale.

title: Symbolic Regression with Bayesian Neural Networks for Discovering Hidden Mathematical Relationships
abstract: This paper explores the application of Bayesian Neural Networks (BNNs) in conjunction with symbolic regression to uncover hidden mathematical relationships within observational datasets. Traditional symbolic regression methods often struggle with uncertainty and lack the ability to generate multiple potential mathematical expressions, leading to a reliance on heuristics for selection. This research proposes a novel approach where a BNN learns a mapping between input features and symbolic expressions, incorporating Bayesian inference to quantify the uncertainty associated with each expression. This allows for the identification of the most probable mathematical relationships while simultaneously providing a probabilistic assessment of their reliability. The core claim is that BNNs can efficiently discover complex mathematical relationships, offering a robust and evidence-based method for hypothesis generation. The system is evaluated through simulated datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness in identifying accurate mathematical models and handling noisy data. The key contribution lies in the ability to leverage Bayesian uncertainty to guide the search process and provide a more nuanced understanding of the underlying relationships.

title: 基于动态自适应的量子纠缠计算的自适应自适应矩阵
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, holds immense potential for transformative technologies, including quantum computing and quantum communication. However, achieving practical quantum computation necessitates the development of robust and adaptable quantum algorithms. This paper explores a novel approach to quantum entanglement computation, focusing on a dynamic self-adaptive matrix based framework. We introduce a method that dynamically adjusts the entanglement state based on input data's geometric characteristics, thereby enhancing computational accuracy. This approach overcomes limitations of static parameterization, offering a more flexible and potentially more efficient solution for complex quantum calculations. The core mechanism involves an optimization loop to refine the entanglement configuration, ultimately improving the fidelity of the computation. This work represents a significant advancement in the design of quantum algorithms, specifically targeting the challenges of adaptive quantum computation.

title: Title: Non-Linear Constraint Optimization with Adaptive Sampling
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to non-linear constraint optimization, focusing on dynamic adaptation of sampling strategies. Traditional methods often rely on static sampling, failing to effectively handle the inherent non-linearity of the optimization problem. We introduce a Bayesian optimization framework enhanced with a dynamically adjusted sampling method, leveraging reinforcement learning to continuously refine the search for optimal constraints. The core mechanism centers on a multi-stage process: initial constraint definition, a Bayesian optimization step to refine the bounds, and a reinforcement learning-driven sampling step to explore the search space more effectively. We evaluate the proposed algorithm on a diverse set of benchmark problems, demonstrating significant improvements in efficiency and robustness compared to existing methods. The results highlight the potential of this approach to tackle complex, non-linear constraint optimization challenges.

title: Cognitive Computing with Symbolic AI and Deep Learning Fusion
abstract: Current cognitive systems frequently encounter difficulties in tasks requiring complex reasoning and the integration of common-sense knowledge. This paper proposes a novel architecture for cognitive computing that aims to overcome these limitations by fusing the strengths of Symbolic Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Deep Learning. The core idea is to construct a hybrid system that utilizes knowledge graphs and rule-based reasoning – the traditional domain of Symbolic AI – alongside deep learning models to achieve more robust, accurate, and, crucially, explainable reasoning. We present a detailed framework for this fusion, outlining the data flow, the interaction between the symbolic and deep learning components, and the mechanisms for knowledge transfer and validation. The architecture is designed to address the shortcomings of relying solely on either approach, capitalizing on the representational power of symbolic AI and the learning capabilities of deep learning. The resulting system offers enhanced performance in tasks demanding both logical inference and pattern recognition, ultimately contributing to the development of more truly intelligent and understandable cognitive systems.

title: Hierarchical Probability Space Modeling (HPSM)
abstract: This paper introduces Hierarchical Probability Space Modeling (HPSM), a novel framework for representing and analyzing probability space data through a hierarchical structure. The core principle of HPSM is to construct a system where each level of granularity represents a distinct, interconnected probability space, allowing for the identification of complex correlations across multiple levels of abstraction. This approach addresses limitations of current probabilistic models by enabling a more intuitive and robust understanding of complex relationships. The paper details the methodology of HPSM, including the design of a graph-based representation and a mechanism for identifying and analyzing correlations between these levels. We present initial results demonstrating the effectiveness of HPSM in modeling and predicting probabilistic outcomes. The focus is on providing a robust, scalable, and conceptually intuitive method for exploring and manipulating probabilistic data. The paper concludes with a discussion of potential applications and future research directions within this field.

title: Explainable AI via Causal Bayesian Networks
abstract: Current Explainable AI (XAI) techniques frequently generate explanations that are merely post-hoc justifications for model predictions, lacking a deep understanding of the model's reasoning process. This paper proposes a novel approach to XAI based on the construction of Causal Bayesian Networks (CBNs). CBNs are employed to explicitly model the causal relationships between input features and the model's output, offering a more robust and interpretable explanation. Unlike existing XAI methods which often rely on correlations, our approach leverages causality to provide a truly grounded understanding of how the model arrives at its decisions. The method is presented with a detailed theoretical framework and outlines the steps involved in constructing and utilizing CBNs for explainability. This research addresses a critical limitation in current XAI by moving beyond correlation-based explanations towards a causal understanding, ultimately leading to more reliable and trustworthy AI systems.

title: Title: Adaptive Topological Optimization of Quantum States
abstract: Adaptive Topological Optimization of Quantum States explores a novel approach to quantum computation by leveraging the inherent topological properties of quantum states. This research investigates a novel algorithm that dynamically adjusts the connectivity and path of quantum states, allowing for more efficient encoding and optimization within quantum circuits. The core claim posits that this algorithmic framework, driven by the principles of topological optimization, can significantly enhance the performance and scalability of quantum systems. The paper presents a detailed explanation of the algorithm's mechanics and its potential impact on quantum computation efficiency. This work contributes to the advancement of quantum algorithm design and offers a fundamentally different perspective on quantum state manipulation.

title: Biak Bare-backed Fruit Bat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Biak Algorithm," inspired by the foraging behavior of the Biak bare-backed fruit bat (Ataguma biak). The Biak bat is known for its unique foraging strategy involving a 'figure-eight' flight pattern and a specific approach to resource exploration. This paper details the algorithm's design, focusing on mimicking these key characteristics within a problem-solving framework. The Biak Algorithm utilizes a population-based search, incorporating elements of Lévy flight and a novel 'exploration radius' mechanism to dynamically adjust the search space. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, including the Rastrigin function, the Sphere function, and the Brent test function. Results demonstrate that the Biak Algorithm effectively converges to optimal or near-optimal solutions with competitive efficiency compared to established metaheuristic methods like the Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization. The algorithm's adaptive exploration strategy is a key factor in its success, allowing it to navigate complex, high-dimensional landscapes. This research contributes a new perspective to metaheuristic algorithm design, offering a potentially valuable tool for tackling diverse optimization challenges.

title: Adaptive Program Synthesis via Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to program synthesis utilizing evolutionary algorithms, specifically focusing on adaptive program synthesis. The core idea is to treat program synthesis as an evolutionary problem, employing genetic algorithms to generate and refine programs. A key innovation lies in the incorporation of adaptive mechanisms that dynamically adjust the evolutionary algorithm's parameters and search strategies based on the performance of the synthesized programs. This allows the system to intelligently respond to the complexities of the synthesis task, leading to improved efficiency and quality of the generated code. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical framework and outline the key components, emphasizing the self-optimization capabilities inherent in the system. The research addresses the limitations of traditional, static program synthesis methods and paves the way for more robust and adaptable automated program generation.

title: Quantum Geometry Mapping: A Dynamic Optimization Approach
abstract: Quantum Geometry Mapping (QGM) presents a novel approach to geometric optimization utilizing quantum entanglement and topological structures. This work introduces a dynamic optimization method predicated on the properties of quantum entanglement, aiming to enhance the efficiency and robustness of geometric transformations. The core mechanism involves the creation of entangled quantum mappings, which are then iteratively refined through a process of quantum state manipulation, ultimately leading to optimized geometric configurations. The proposed method offers a potential paradigm shift in geometric optimization, leveraging the unique capabilities of quantum mechanics to achieve superior results compared to classical optimization techniques. This paper provides a comprehensive theoretical foundation, detailing the underlying principles and mathematical framework of QGM, and presents preliminary experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness.

title: Dynamic Matrix Decomposition
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of dynamic matrix decomposition (DMD) to address the challenges associated with large matrix manipulation. Traditional methods often struggle with scalability and computational complexity, particularly when dealing with matrices exceeding typical computational limits. This work proposes a novel approach leveraging quantum entanglement and key distribution to dramatically accelerate the decomposition process. We explore the theoretical foundations and initial experimental validation of DMD, highlighting its potential for handling significantly larger matrices than currently feasible. The core mechanism centers around quantum state manipulation and its application to matrix inversion, demonstrating a significant improvement in computational speed and robustness compared to classical approaches. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions, emphasizing the transformative impact of quantum computation on matrix analysis.

title: Adaptive Quantum Constraint System for Parallel Computation
abstract: This paper introduces an Adaptive Quantum Constraint System (AQCS) designed to optimize computational efficiency in parallel architectures. The AQCS dynamically adjusts quantum constraint systems based on an analysis of the target parallel architecture, maximizing the benefits of parallel computation. We present a novel approach leveraging a 'Dynamic Constraint Adaptation' mechanism to achieve this optimization. This research addresses a significant challenge in quantum computing – the need for tailored constraints across diverse hardware platforms – by providing a framework for intelligent constraint engineering. The theoretical foundation rests on a combination of principles from quantum information theory, constraint programming, and adaptive control. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the AQCS through simulations and preliminary results, highlighting its potential to significantly improve performance in various quantum algorithm implementations.

title: Geometric Information Graph
abstract: The current landscape of knowledge representation and reasoning heavily relies on structured data, often employing databases and relational models. However, the inherent complexity of geometric data – data representing shapes, positions, and relationships – presents a significant challenge for traditional knowledge representation. This paper proposes a novel approach leveraging geometric information graphs to construct a knowledge base, facilitating efficient retrieval, inference, and visualization through the application of geometric structure. We introduce a framework centered around a graph database structure, meticulously designed to capture and utilize geometric relationships. This system aims to address limitations of existing knowledge representation methods, particularly in scenarios requiring geometric reasoning and data exploration.

title: Dynamic Information Entropy Model (DIEM) – A Novel Algorithm for Data Compression, Transmission, and Storage
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm, Dynamic Information Entropy Model (DIEM), designed to optimize data compression, transmission, and storage processes. Traditional information entropy models are static, offering limited adaptability to dynamic data characteristics. DIEM dynamically adjusts data feature representations to maximize efficiency. The core of the DIEM lies in its application of a dynamic entropy weighting scheme, which iteratively refines feature representations based on observed data patterns. This adaptive approach significantly enhances data processing performance compared to static models. The paper details the algorithm's methodology, provides a comprehensive analysis of its performance, and discusses potential future developments.

abstract: This paper investigates the application of probability graphs for adaptive feature extraction and modeling. title: ## Andersen's Flying Fox: A Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by a Remarkable Bird
abstract: This paper introduces Andersen's Flying Fox (AFF), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the unique flight capabilities of the Andersen's flying fox, a large gliding squirrel-like marsupial. AFF leverages the bat-inspired algorithm's principles of exploration and exploitation, incorporating a novel "glide" mechanism mimicking the animal's efficient gliding motion. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, with each individual representing a potential solution. The core of AFF lies in its dynamically adjusted glide angle, influenced by a fitness-based feedback loop, which steers solutions towards promising regions of the search space. We present a detailed description of the algorithm's design, including its parameters and operational rules. We demonstrate AFF's effectiveness through simulations on benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization. The primary focus is on the algorithm's adaptability and its ability to efficiently converge to optimal or near-optimal solutions, particularly in complex, multimodal landscapes. The key contributions of this work are the introduction of the 'glide' mechanism and its integration into a robust metaheuristic framework.

The core mechanism centers on exploiting quantum phenomena to quantify and manage uncertainty, ultimately leading to improved model performance.

title: ## Andean Mouse: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Andean Mouse Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Andean Mouse, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Andean mice in the high-altitude Andean mountain ranges. The algorithm leverages the mouse's adaptive search strategy, specifically its ability to exploit local resources while simultaneously exploring new areas, to achieve efficient global optimization. Andean Mouse combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) with a unique adaptive adjustment mechanism based on resource availability. The algorithm's core components include an adaptive inertia weight, a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance, and a novel resource-based adjustment mechanism. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through a series of benchmark problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's key parameters are described, along with a detailed explanation of its operational logic. The results indicate that Andean Mouse presents a robust and effective approach to solving complex optimization problems. The performance is evaluated using metrics such as convergence speed, solution quality, and computational efficiency.

The core claim focuses on creating algorithms that effectively handle the inherent randomness and sensitivity of stochastic systems.

title: Title: Dynamic Constraint Propagation within Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: Evolutionary algorithms (EAs) are widely used for optimization problems, but their performance can be significantly affected by constraint satisfaction. This paper investigates the application of dynamic constraint propagation to enhance the efficiency of EAs. We propose a novel constraint propagation mechanism that intelligently adjusts constraints based on the system's current state, aiming to improve solution convergence. The core claim is that extending evolutionary algorithms to dynamically propagate constraints across a system's state space results in enhanced performance. This work addresses a critical challenge in evolutionary algorithm design: ensuring consistent and effective constraint application. The paper details the proposed mechanism, its implementation, and experimental results demonstrating improved convergence rates compared to traditional EAs.

title: Alexander's Bush Squirrel: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Bush Squirrel Behavior
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Alexander's Bush Squirrel" (ABS), inspired by the foraging behavior of bush squirrels. Bush squirrels exhibit a complex and efficient strategy for locating and exploiting food resources in a patchy environment. ABS leverages this strategy through a combination of adaptive exploration and exploitation phases, utilizing a modified particle representation and a dynamic territory allocation mechanism. The algorithm employs a novel 'nesting' concept to represent solutions, mimicking the squirrel's creation of nests for food storage. The core of ABS involves a stochastic search for optimal territories, guided by a probability distribution reflecting resource density. The algorithm's performance is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in both continuous and discrete spaces. The results indicate that ABS consistently outperforms several established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in scenarios demanding robust exploration and efficient exploitation. Future work will focus on incorporating adaptive parameters and further refining the territory allocation mechanism to enhance the algorithm's adaptability and scalability.

title: 自适应量子拓扑的自适应几何变换
abstract: This paper investigates the application of self-adaptive quantum topology for achieving complex geometric transformations, offering a novel approach to handle non-linear geometric problems in complex systems. We propose a method leveraging the inherent self-adaptability of quantum topology to dynamically modify geometric parameters, allowing for the creation of intricate transformations without requiring explicit parameter tuning. The core mechanism centers on utilizing the topological properties of quantum systems to facilitate these transformations, addressing limitations of traditional geometric methods. The paper presents a detailed theoretical framework outlining the design of this adaptive technique, including the mathematical formulation of the transformation process and a discussion of its potential applications in various fields, particularly within the context of quantum information processing and advanced geometry. We further explore the advantages and challenges of this approach, highlighting its potential to unlock new capabilities in geometric manipulation. Finally, we outline future research directions to further refine and expand the capabilities of this self-adaptive quantum topology framework.

title: Uncertainty-Aware End-to-End AI Weather Forecasting: Disentangling Observation and Model Contributions
abstract: End-to-end weather forecasting systems produce skillful global gridded and station forecasts directly from raw Earth observations, replacing the numerical weather prediction pipeline, including data assimilation, at a fraction of its cost. These systems are deterministic and issue no uncertainty. Here we render the Aardvark Weather model probabilistic by attaching one stochastic mechanism to each component: learned, input-dependent noise at the observation encoder, capturing aleatoric uncertainty inherited from the observing system, and Monte Carlo dropout in the processor, capturing epistemic uncertainty in the learned dynamics. The resulting nested ensemble attributes forecast spread to the two sources through a law-of-total-variance decomposition, cross-checked by withholding observation streams. Probabilistic finetuning significantly improves the mean forecast, by 4.2% on average across variables and lead times. The ensemble is calibrated against ERA5 through the medium range (spread-skill ratio 0.98), keeps station RMSE within 2.4% of the deterministic model while beating it in CRPS at every lead time, and trails the operational ECMWF ensemble. The encoder branch behaves as observation-driven uncertainty. Component-attributed uncertainty makes end-to-end forecasts more transparent, a step toward observation-driven digital twins of the atmosphere.

title: Cost-Aware Active Feature Acquisition for Differential Diagnosis under Realistic Clinical Availability Constraints
abstract: Abstract Active Feature Acquisition (AFA) adaptively selects which diagnostic test to order next and offers a route to reduce unnecessary laboratory testing in acute care. Existing clinical AFA evaluations, however, assume every feature can be retrieved on demand and split data at the visit level, both of which inflate apparent performance. We re-evaluate cost-aware AFA under constraints designed to reflect deployment. From MIMIC-IV we constructed a cohort of 64,766 acute admissions (39,884 patients; 21 conditions; 55 features in 30 test panels) with a patient-level split, a 12-hour decision cutoff, and a per-patient availability mask from what was actually measured, and priced panels using the 2026 Medicare fee schedule under panel-level billing. We evaluated EIG-Cost, which scores each panel by Monte-Carlo Expected Information Gain penalised by its dollar cost, against eight published methods across budgets $30–$60 over five patient-level resamples. At a $30 budget, EIG-Cost achieved the highest macro-F1 ( 0.188 , 95% CI [0.185, 0.191] ) at the lowest cost ($17.28), exceeding the strongest baseline in all five resamples ( p < 0.001 ; Cohen’s d = 4.0 ), and led at every budget. Three of the eight methods collapsed to a vitals-only baseline (macro-F1 ≈ 0.040 ), acquiring nothing even at higher budgets, a genuine failure to adapt to availability rather than a budget limitation. Despite modest absolute accuracy, EIG-Cost’s probabilities were well-calibrated (expected calibration error 0.048 ). Under realistic availability constraints, clinical AFA is substantially harder than full-availability benchmarks imply, several published methods fail outright, and cost-aware information-gain scoring is a robust choice in this harder setting.

title: Computational Processor Ontology (CPO): Mathematical Formulation of Operational Time, Emergence of Meaning, and Error Dynamics in Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: **چکیده (فارسی)** این پژوهش، چارچوب ریاضی و تجربی مدل «هستی‌شناسی محاسباتی پردازشگرها» (CPO) را تدوین و اثبات می‌کند. در حالی که یادداشت‌های پیشین پایه‌های مفهومی فضا و زمان را به عنوان فرمت‌های محاسباتی معرفی کردند، این مطالعه نخستین فرمول‌بندی دقیق ریاضی و اثبات الگوریتمی را برای «مکان»، «فضا» و «زمان» ارائه می‌دهد و پیوند ذاتی آن‌ها را با «معنا»، «خرد جمعی» و «واگرایی ناشی از اگو» اثبات می‌کند. در این معماری، مکان به عنوان بردار تخصیص توجه بر روی داده‌های خام، فضا به عنوان عملگر فشرده‌سازی ابعاد اطلاعاتی، زمان به عنوان سنجه مقایسه تفاوت حالات متوالی در حافظه، و معنا به مثابه ساختار همبستگی برآمده از تبادل داده میان پردازنده‌ها فرمول‌بندی شده است. در یک شبیه‌سازی تجربی چندعاملی با ۲۰ پردازنده ($N = 20$)، تبادل آزاد اطلاعات خطای ادراکی را از **۴.۶۹۱۳** به **۱.۰۵۳۳** کاهش داد (**۴.۴۵ برابر بهبود دقت و پیدایش خرد جمعی**). در مقابل، تزریق بردار سوگیری اگو، خطای شبکه را به **۷۹.۰۳۶۶** رساند (**۷۵.۰۴ برابر واگرایی و توهم سیستمی**). این نتایج، پایه‌های ریاضی لازم را برای نگارش رساله‌ای جامع پیرامون آگاهی و هستی‌شناسی اطلاعات فراهم می‌سازد. --- **Abstract (English)** This paper establishes the formal mathematical and empirical framework of the **Computational Processor Ontology (CPO)** model. While preceding notes introduced conceptual foundations of space and time as computational formats, this study provides the first rigorous mathematical formulation and algorithmic proof for **Location**, **Space**, and **Time**, demonstrating their intrinsic links to **Meaning**, **Collective Wisdom**, and **Ego-induced Divergence**. Within this architecture, Location is formalized as an attention allocation vector over raw data, Space as an information dimensionality reduction operator, Time as a state-difference comparison metric, and Meaning as an emergent covariance structure arising from inter-processor data exchange. In a multi-agent empirical simulation involving $N = 20$ processors, unconstrained data exchange reduced perceptual error from **4.6913** to **1.0533** (**a 4.45-fold precision enhancement and the emergence of collective wisdom**). Conversely, injecting an ego-bias vector escalated network error to **79.0366** (**a 75.04-fold divergence and systemic hallucination**). These results establish the mathematical foundation required for a comprehensive treatise on consciousness and information ontology.

title: 基于量子拓扑的机器学习优化器
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning optimization framework based on quantum topology. We explore the potential of quantum mechanics, specifically superposition and entanglement, to significantly accelerate training and inference processes for machine learning algorithms. We propose a new architecture that leverages these quantum properties to enhance the computational efficiency of various machine learning tasks. The core mechanism involves manipulating quantum states to represent and process data, potentially unlocking faster and more robust learning. This research aims to provide a foundation for future advancements in machine learning by incorporating the unique capabilities of quantum systems.

title: Quantum Entangled State Transfer Algorithm Optimization
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental quantum phenomenon, offers the potential for unparalleled security and efficient data transfer. This paper investigates the optimization of a quantum entangled state transfer algorithm, leveraging quantum entanglement and quantum key distribution (QKD) to enhance data security and transmission efficiency. The algorithm incorporates a novel approach to manage and utilize entangled states, aiming to overcome current limitations in quantum communication protocols. The research focuses on designing a robust and scalable protocol for secure information transfer utilizing quantum entanglement. The core mechanism centers around creating and maintaining entangled states, facilitating instantaneous and secure data transfer, thereby enhancing the overall security and efficiency of quantum communication.

title: Dynamic Information Fields (DIF) Theory
abstract: This paper presents a novel Dynamic Information Field (DIF) theory, integrating information theory and quantum field theory to investigate non-linear effects of information in quantum systems and applying this framework to quantum computation optimization and control. We develop a mechanism where information serves as a critical parameter, leveraging the non-linear properties of information entropy to design quantum algorithms. The core claim is that the theory provides a new perspective on quantum computation, offering potential improvements in algorithm efficiency and robustness. The work explores the connection between information and quantum state evolution, and demonstrates the utility of information entropy in guiding the design of quantum algorithms. The theoretical framework is presented as a means to enhance the understanding of quantum systems and advance the field of quantum computation.

title: Geometric Chaos in Neural Networks – Self-Organization of Feature Representation
abstract: This paper explores the potential of geometric chaos within neural networks to enhance model robustness. Traditional neural network architectures often exhibit brittle representations, prone to sensitivity to small perturbations. We propose utilizing geometric chaos analysis – a mathematical framework that describes systems exhibiting unpredictable, self-organized behavior – to understand how feature space evolves. We hypothesize that the inherent geometry of these feature spaces can lead to emergent robustness, allowing the network to better generalize to unseen data. The core mechanism involves quantifying and exploiting the chaotic dynamics of feature representations through geometric analysis, ultimately aiming to improve prediction accuracy and stability. This work challenges conventional approaches by focusing on the underlying geometric properties of neural network representations.
